He, glory be to Him, is most knowing of who deserves to bear the message, and He is the All-Wise who leaves nothing to futility; He is the One who decrees every matter so that it accords with what is right.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says thereafter:

﴿Indeed, in Yusuf and his brothers are signs for those who ask.(7)﴾

1 - al-Judb: drought, the opposite of fertility. A "jadiyyah" land is one with neither little nor much (vegetation), neither pasture nor herbage; a "mujdab" land is one that hardly ever becomes fertile. [Lisan al-Arab, root j-d-b].
2 - al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir [4/345], ﴿And complete His favour upon you..(6)﴾ [Yusuf]: i.e., with prophethood; it was also said: by bringing your brothers to you; and it was said: by saving you from every hardship."
3 - Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah took Ibrahim as a khalil (intimate friend)(125)﴾ [al-Nisa']. Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was named Khalil Allah because of his intense love for his Lord, mighty and majestic, due to the obedience he performed for Him which He loves and is pleased with. [Ibn Kathir 1/560].

That is, Yusuf became a vessel (*zarf*) for events, because "fi" (in) indicates containment (*zarfiyya*, the sense of place or time). The meaning of containment is that there is something within which another thing is contained, so it is as if Yusuf became the centre around which events would revolve, through the people who took part in them.

"Yusuf" is a non-Arabic (*a'jamiyy*) name, and for that reason it is a diptote (*mamnu' min al-sarf*), meaning it does not take tanween (nunation, the final "-n" sound). So we do not say *fi Yusufin* but *fi Yusuf*.

﴿Yusuf and his brothers are signs for those who ask﴾ [Yusuf].

This means that what happened points to the power of God, glorified is He. He was thrown into the well and was rescued so that he might be raised in the most distinguished house in Egypt.

We know that the word *ayah* (sign) is applied to a wondrous matter that draws attention. In the Qur'an it carries three meanings:

The first is the cosmic sign (*ayah kawniyya*), such as the sun, the moon, the night and the day. These cosmic signs are a store of material for reflection that leads to faith in the Necessary Existent (*wajib al-wujud*), who is God, glorified is He. When you see the cosmos ordered with such utmost precision, you must reflect on the necessity of a Creator for this cosmos.

The second wondrous sign is the miracles that break the laws of nature (*nawamis*), which the messengers bring to demonstrate the truthfulness of their message from God, such as the fire that became cool and safe for Ibrahim, and the water that split and became like a mighty mountain before the staff of Musa.

There is a third meaning of the word *ayah*, which refers to the verses of the Noble Qur'an.

In the words of the Truthful God, glorified is He:

﴿There was certainly in Yusuf and his brothers signs for those who ask﴾ [Yusuf].

From this we draw the lesson from everything that happened to Yusuf, whom his brothers plotted against in order to be rid of him; but their scheme turned out to Yusuf's benefit.

In all of this there is consolation (*salwa*) for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to strengthen his heart. So let him not be grieved by the persecution of his people, their conspiring against him, their desire to exile him to Syria, their attempts to kill him, and their attempts to boycott him; and after that they came to live under the shade of his protection.

So then: do not despair, O Muhammad, for God is your Helper by His permission and power, and do not be impatient for God's help, you and those with you, as came in the Qur'an:

﴿Do you think that you will enter Paradise without the example of those who passed away before you? Adversity and hardship touched them, and they were shaken, until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of God?" Unquestionably, the help of God is near﴾ [al-Baqarah].

The Truthful God then explains what happened to Yusuf after the humiliation that befell him from his brothers, and time passes until the good vision that Yusuf, peace be upon him, had is fulfilled.

It is said that the vision of Yusuf was fulfilled within a period ranging between forty years and eighty years.

For this reason we find that the vision of good takes a long time to be confirmed, whereas the vision of evil comes quickly; for it is a mercy of God that a vision of evil occurs and comes to an end, because if it remained unfulfilled for a long time, a person would fall prey to imagining evil in all its forms.

Evil comes in only one form, but good has many forms; so God makes you imagine what good will come to you in varied colours and interpretations.

The example of a call for evil is the supplication of Musa against the people of Pharaoh, when he said:

﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus].

The Truthful God says:

﴿There was certainly in Yusuf and his brothers signs for those who ask﴾ [Yusuf].

So every day of that story contains a sign, and the signs are gathered together.

There is another reading: "There was certainly in Yusuf and his brothers *a* sign for those who ask", meaning that the whole story, with all its details and events, is one wondrous sign.

The Truthful God has given us in the Qur'an an example of gathering many signs into one sign, as He said:

﴿And We made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign...﴾ [al-Mu'minun].

Although each of them is a single sign on its own.

You may view the whole story of Yusuf as one wondrous sign that includes all its scenes, or you may view each scene as a sign in itself.

The Truthful God says at the end of this verse that the story is:

﴿signs for those who ask﴾ [Yusuf].

The askers here are either the polytheists, whom the Jews incited to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the matter of Yusuf, or Muslims who seek lessons from earlier nations. The revelation came down upon the unlettered Messenger with this sūrah in an eloquent, miraculous form that no human being can match.

When you recite the sūrah, it may take you twenty minutes. Bring any person to speak for a third of an hour and remain retaining what he said; you will not find anyone who does that. But the Truthful God said to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace:

﴿We will make you recite, and you will not forget﴾ [al-A'la].

So we find the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, memorising what was sent down to him from his Lord, dictating it to his companions, leading them in prayer, and reciting in prayer what was revealed to him. Although the Qur'an contains similar verses (*mutashabihat*), he, may God bless him and grant him peace, never made a mistake once while reciting the Qur'an.

The examples are many, among them the words of the Truth:

﴿And be patient over what has afflicted you. Indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [Luqman].

And again He says:

﴿Indeed, that is of the matters of determination﴾ [al-Shura].

Likewise the words of the Truthful God:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs﴾ [al-Hijr].

And in another place the Truth says:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and bliss﴾ [al-Tur].

How could an unlettered human being recall all of that, were it not that the One who sent down the revelation to him willed it for him?

Then the Truthful God says:

﴿When they said, "Yusuf and his brother are more beloved to our father than we, though we are a group. Indeed, our father is in manifest error"﴾ [Yusuf].

1 - Ibn Hisham al-Ansari said in *Mughni al-Labib* [1/144]: "*Fi* is a preposition with ten meanings, among them *zarfiyya*, which is either of place or of time. Both have been combined in the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land; but they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years...﴾ [al-Rum]."

2 - This is in the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "Burn him and support your gods, if you are to act." We said, "O fire, be cool and safe upon Ibrahim."﴾ [al-Anbiya']. *Al-barad* is the opposite of heat, and *al-burudah* is the opposite of warmth. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: that is, it should not harm him. Ibn 'Abbas and Abu al-'Aliyah said: had God not said, "and safety" [al-Anbiya' 69], it would have harmed Ibrahim with its coldness. Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, said: [when God said] "be cool and safe upon Ibrahim" [al-Anbiya' 69], they said: place for him an enclosure of thick firewood and set fire to it from every side; he rose in the morning and nothing of it had touched him, until God extinguished it. [See Ibn Kathir's *Tafsir* 3/184.]

3 - *Al-tawd*: a firm, high mountain. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿So it split, and each part became like a great mountain﴾ [al-Shu'ara'].

4 - *Sallanī min hammī*: he consoled me, and *aslānī*: he removed it from me; *insalla 'anni al-hamm* and *tasalla* mean: the grief was lifted. [Lisan al-'Arab, root s-l-w.]

5 - *Al-ba'sa'*: poverty and hardship. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And the patient in adversity and hardship...﴾ [al-Baqarah 177], in times of poverty and need. *Al-darra'*: prolonged illness, or any hardship, or loss of wealth or lives; this is painful and sorrowful, and it is the opposite of *al-sarra'*. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/53, 292.]

6 - "Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi said, on the authority of Sulayman: there were forty years between Yusuf's vision and its interpretation. Al-Hasan said: from the time Yusuf parted from Ya'qub until they reunited was eighty years, during which grief did not leave his heart, and his tears flowed down his cheeks." This agrees with what Ibn Kathir said in his *Tafsir* [2/491].

7 - *Tams al-shay'*: its form changed or its trace was effaced. *Tamasahu ghayruh*: he disfigured or erased it and removed it. *Tamasa 'aynahu*: he blinded it; *tamasa 'ala 'aynihi*: he blinded it, implying the meaning of covering and veiling them. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes...﴾ [Ya-Sin 66]. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/406, abridged.]

8 - *Shaddahu*: he strengthened it; *shadda al-habl*: he tied it very firmly; *shadda asrahu*: he strengthened its bond and made its fetter secure so that he never escapes from it, that is, he firmly controlled him. ﴿And We strengthened their captivity...﴾ [al-Insan 28], meaning We made their bonds secure and controlled them. And His words ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom...﴾ [Sad 20] mean We strengthened it. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/343, 344, adapted.]

9 - That is, He, glorified is He, made her a sign for people, a decisive proof of His power over whatever He wills: He created Adam without father or mother, created Hawwa' from a male without a female, created 'Isa from a female without a male, and created the rest of humanity from a male and a female. Said by Ibn Kathir in his *Tafsir* of this verse [3/246].

10 - Al-Qurtubi said in his *Tafsir* [4/3450]: "That is: indeed there was a sign for those who asked about the news of Yusuf in what they were informed of, for they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Makkah, saying: tell us about a man among the prophets who was in Syria, who sent his son to Egypt, and wept for him until he went blind? There was no one in Makkah from the People of the Book, nor anyone who knew the news of the prophets. Rather, the Jews from Madinah directed them to ask about this. So God, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down the sūrah of Yusuf all at once, containing everything in the Torah and more, and that was a sign for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the same way as the raising of 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, of the dead."

11 - *'Azm al-amr*: figuratively, it means that the matter was carried out with a strong resolve from its doer. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And when the matter is resolved...﴾ [Muhammad 21]: an intransitive verb, meaning it was carried out, settled and established with a strong resolve from you. And God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And if they resolve upon divorce...﴾ [al-Baqarah 227], meaning they formed the intention to complete it. And God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, that is of the matters of resolve﴾ [Al 'Imran 186], meaning: among the serious, right matters in which hesitation is not permissible, or among the great matters that people of strong resolve carry out. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/20.]

12 - *Al-'usbah*: a close-knit group. God, the Exalted, relates the words of Yusuf's brothers: ﴿while we are a group [usbah]﴾ [Yusuf 8]. *'Asabahu*: he bound it tightly. And His words ﴿This is a difficult day﴾ [Hud 77] mean one of severe binding, which binds people and constricts them, or severe heat, severe terror. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/22.]

13 - *Al-dalal*: forgetfulness and loss; *dalal* may also be used for doing what is less than the best, as in His words in the story of Yusuf: ﴿Indeed, you are in your old error﴾ [Yusuf 95], meaning: the intensity of your attachment to Yusuf and your grief over him, which in their view is error. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/395.]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (*Tafsir al-Sha'rawi*, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 12, verse 8:

We must here consider brotherhood in its types. Brothers may be full brothers, sharing both parents. They may share only the father and not the mother, or only the mother and not the father. The number of Ya'qub's sons, peace be upon him, was twelve: seven from one wife, and four from two women, Zilfa and Bilha. Two were from Rahil: Yusuf and his brother Binyamin.

The verse we are reflecting on begins:

﴿When they said: Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we are, though we are a group... (8)﴾ [Yusuf]

The *lam* that precedes the name Yusuf is for emphasis, as if they had said: "By Allah, our father loves Yusuf and his brother more than he loves us." Emphasis is used only in response to denial.

This shows that they disagreed about the matter of Yusuf, peace be upon him. One of them wanted to take revenge on Yusuf, and another proposed easing the matter by casting him into a well (*jubb*)(2). Then they agreed that Yusuf was dearer to their father than they were.

In their statement there is a glimmer of fairness, for they acknowledged their father's love for them. But their saying contains some of the heedlessness of human beings, because they should have sought the reason for their father's increased love for Yusuf and his brother.

Yusuf and his brother were young children, and their mother had died(3). Only the father remained for them, and he felt the necessity of combining in himself toward them both a father's tenderness and a mother's tenderness. Because they were small, we find the father bending over them with the capacity for care that Allah had placed in his heart.

This is a matter over which Ya'qub had no control. Rather, it is a divine matter that Allah placed in hearts without choice, and He places it even in the hearts of animals.

Allah, glorified is He, willed to make tenderness proportionate to need. For example, if anyone approaches a cat's newborn kittens, she attacks the one who approaches her young.

For this reason, the ancient Arab answered a man who asked him, "Which of your children do you love most?" He said: "The young one until he grows up, the absent one until he returns, and the sick one until he recovers."

We see this matter in our daily lives. We find a woman who has two sons: one whom Allah has blessed with abundant provision and who takes care of all her affairs and needs, and the other who lives in sufficiency(4) or on his brother's help. We find that her heart is always with the weak one.

Therefore we say: love is an emotional matter that is not subject to regulation, and there is no obligation regarding it. When the Qur'an addresses it, the Truth, glorified is He, clarifies that love and hatred are natural emotions(5). So love whom you wish and hate whom you wish, but beware of wronging people because of whom you love or whom you hate.

Read the word of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to piety. (8)﴾ [al-Ma'ida]

So love whom you wish and hate whom you wish, but do not wrong anyone because of love or hatred.

Someone may say: "But the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: 'None of you believes until I am dearer to him than himself.'"

We say: Read what came in the same narration of the hadith. 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, with his clarity, frankness and boldness, without hypocrisy, said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love you more than my wealth and my children, but as for myself, no." The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, repeated his saying: "None of you believes until I am dearer to him than himself."(8)

'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, understood that the matter is a doctrinal and obligatory commitment, and he understood that what is required is love of the intellect, not love of emotion.

Love of the intellect, as we know, is to perceive a beneficial matter and do it, just as one takes a bitter medicine. You do this out of intellectual love, desiring that the Truth grant healing.

The Muslim loves the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with his intellect, because he knows that had the Messenger of Allah not come, he would not have known the sweetness of faith. The Muslim may rise in love for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, until the love of the Messenger becomes emotional love in his heart.

Thus we see that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, has clarified for us the dividing lines between the principles of intellectual love and emotional love.

Another example from 'Umar's biography on the same matter, intellectual love and emotional love, is when the killer of his brother passed by him. One of those sitting with him said: "This is the killer of your brother." 'Umar said: "And what shall I do with him, when Allah has guided him to Islam?"

'Umar turned his face away from his brother's killer. The man came to him and said: "Why do you turn your face away from me?" 'Umar said: "Because I do not love you, for you are the killer of my brother." The man said: "Does your not loving me prevent me from any of my rights?" 'Umar said: "No." The man said: "It is for you to love whom you wish and dislike whom you wish, and only women weep over love."

The brothers of Yusuf should have noticed that their father's love for Yusuf and his brother was a natural emotion for which the father should not be held accountable, because the circumstances of the two boys compelled him to love them with this love.

The story continues with its escalation of good and its escalation of evil. One may ask: "Why was their anger focused on Yusuf alone?"

It is said that they did not want to grieve their father with the loss of both of them, Yusuf and his brother, or that something of Yusuf's dream had leaked to them.

It is remarkable that after this they say:

﴿...while we are a group. (8)﴾ [Yusuf]

A *'usba* (group) is ten or more. *'Usba* also means those who support one another and are zealous for one another, who take care of the interests and meet the needs. Their father had retired and left them the management of the family's affairs.

They said: "Since we manage the family's interests, it was necessary for our father to favor us with love." They did not notice that they were a group, and this is what made the father love them, but he gave greater care to those who were not a group. However, they were heedless in their error and reached an illogical conclusion, which was their saying:

﴿Indeed our father is in clear error. (8)﴾ [Yusuf]

This saying is a conclusion that does not follow from its premises. Yusuf and his brother were two children whose mother had died, and the father must incline toward them with compassion. His love for them did not prevent his love for the grown sons who were able to rely on themselves.

When they say:

﴿Indeed our father is in clear error. (8)﴾ [Yusuf]

some people may understand the word *dalal* (error) here in its broad sense.

We say: No. There is a deliberate error, which is that a person knows the path of truth and goes to falsehood, and this is blameworthy error.

And there is unintentional error, like the error of a man who walks and takes roads he does not know, so he strays from his destination, or like one who forgets some of the truth.

The Almighty said:

﴿That if one of them errs, the other may remind her... (282)﴾ [al-Baqara]

And He, glorified is He, also said:

﴿And He found you lost and guided you. (7)﴾ [al-Duha]

So, blameworthy error is that you know the path of truth and go astray.

Thus the brothers of Yusuf erred in assessing the matter of their father's love for Yusuf and his brother, and they reached a harmful conclusion, because the premises on which they built that conclusion were false. Had they examined the premises with careful scrutiny, they would not have reached the wrong conclusion they stated:

﴿Indeed our father is in clear error. (8)﴾ [Yusuf]

After that, the Truth, glorified is He, mentions what came from the tongues of Yusuf's brothers:

﴿Kill Yusuf or cast him out to some land, so that your father's face will be free for you, and you will be a righteous people after him. (9)﴾

1 - Al-Qurtubi said in his *tafsir* (commentary) [4/3451]: "Their names: Ruben, who was the eldest; Shim'un, Levi, Yahuda, Zabulun, and Yasakhar. Their mother was Lea, daughter of Layan, who was the daughter of Ya'qub's maternal uncle. He had four sons by two concubines: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. Then Lea died, and Ya'qub married her sister Rahil, who bore him Yusuf and Binyamin. So the sons of Ya'qub were twelve men." Al-Suhayli said: "The name of Ya'qub's mother is Rafqa, and Rahil died in childbirth with Binyamin." It was also said regarding the names of the two concubines, Lea and Talta: one of them belonged to Rahil and the other to her sister Lea.

2 - *Jubb*: a well that has not been lined with stones. Al-Layth said: it is a well that is not deep. Al-Farra' said: a well whose interior is vaulted, when its middle is the widest part and is arched. [*Lisan al-'Arab*, root: *jabb*]

3 - Their mother Rahil died in childbirth with Binyamin, as mentioned by al-Qurtubi in his *tafsir*.

4 - *Kafaf*: that is, there is no surplus in his provision; he has only what restrains him from needing people. Al-Jawhari said: *kafaf* of a thing, with a fatha, is its like and equal. *Kafaf* also refers to provision: subsistence, which is what keeps one from needing people, i.e., enough, so that it does not exceed what one needs. [*Lisan al-'Arab*, root: *kafaf*]

5 - *Tab'* and *tabi'a*: the creation and disposition with which a human being is made; *tiba'* is like *tabi'a*, and it is feminine. [*Lisan al-'Arab*, root: *taba'*]

6 - *Jarama al-shay'*, *jurman*: he cut it, and the term came to be applied to doing evil. It is said: *jarama*: he sinned and committed a crime; *jurm al-mal*: he earned wealth in any way; *jarramahu*: he drove him to commit an evil act or sin. The Almighty said: "﴿And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just... (8)﴾ [al-Ma'ida]," meaning: do not let hatred of a people lead you to not be just; i.e., adhere to justice even with those you dislike; be always just, for justice is nearer to piety. [*al-Qamus al-Qawim* 1/121]

7 - *Shana'ahu* and *shana'ahu*, *shan'an*, *sha'natan*, *shanaan*: he hated him and disliked him. The Almighty said: "﴿And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just... (8)﴾ [al-Ma'ida]." *Shani'*: the active participle. The Almighty said: "﴿Indeed, your hater is the one cut off (3)﴾ [al-Kawthar], i.e., the one who hates and detests you. [*al-Qamus al-Qawim* 1/357]

8 - Narrated from the grandfather of Zuhra ibn Ma'bad, who said: "We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was holding the hand of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. 'Umar said: 'By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, you are dearer to me than everything except myself.' The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: 'By Him in whose hand my soul is, none of you believes until I am dearer to him than himself.' 'Umar said: 'Now, by Allah, you are dearer to me than myself.' The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Now, O 'Umar.'" Narrated by Ahmad in his *Musnad* [4/336].

9 - *Al-sumuw*: elevation and height. *Sama al-shay'* *yasmu sumuwan*: it rose. *Tasamaw*: they competed, and *tasamiha*: its competition and boasting. *Al-tasammi*: rank and ascent. [*Lisan al-'Arab*, root: *sama*], adapted.

10 - *Al-fajii'a*: a painful calamity. *Faja'ahu al-musiba*: the calamity pained him. *Al-fawajie*: painful calamities that grieve a person in what is dear to him, of wealth or a close relative; singular *fajia*. [*Lisan al-'Arab*, root: *faja'*]

11 - *Al-sadir*: the bewildered one, and also the one who does not care about anything and does not mind what he does. [*Lisan al-'Arab*, root: *sadar*]

12 - *Al-ghayy*: error and failure. *Ghawa*: he went astray; *al-ghiwaya*: persistence in error; *al-ghawi*: one who is extremely misguided and erring; *aghwahu*: he misled him and brought him into error and deviation. [*al-Qamus al-Qawim* 2/64]

13 - *Tarh al-shay'* and *taraha bihi*: he threw it. *Al-tarh* (with a vowel): distance, and a remote place. The Almighty said: "﴿Or cast him out to some land (9)﴾ [Yusuf]," i.e., throw him into a distant land. [*al-Qamus al-Qawim* 1/399]

14 - *Khala* *fulan ila fulan*: he devoted himself to him and did not occupy himself with anyone else. The Almighty said, on the tongue of Yusuf's brothers: "﴿So that your father's face will be free for you (9)﴾ [Yusuf]," i.e., your father will be free for you, and will turn to you with all his care, and will not be occupied with anyone other than you. [*al-Qamus al-Qawim* 1/209]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 12, verse 9:

Killing is the peak of the evil they considered; and because they were of the Asbat (the tribes), the evil descended to a lesser level, so they said: ﴿Or cast him out to some land...﴾ [Yusuf: 9]

It is as if they feared the sin of killing, and they thought that by this they would be alone in their father's love, for they said: ﴿...that the face of your father may be clear for you...﴾ [Yusuf: 9]

The face is that by which confrontation, smiling and tenderness are accomplished, and it is that on which emotions appear.

What is meant by ﴿...that the face of your father may be clear for you...﴾ [Yusuf: 9] is that there be no obstacle between you and your father.

And their saying ﴿...and after him you will be a righteous people﴾ [Yusuf: 9]

means: they appreciate righteousness, and they know that what they had planned is unacceptable by the standards of righteousness; therefore they said that they would repent after that.

But: what made them know that they would live until they repent? By this saying they forgot that the matter of death is hidden so that no one commits sins and major wrongs.

Or: what may be meant by ﴿a righteous people﴾ [Yusuf: 9]

is that they would be fit for the movement of life, and that their relationship with their father would not be troubled; for when his face is clear for them, they would be at ease, knowing that their father would be just among them and give them all his love, so they would be at rest.

Or what may be meant by ﴿a righteous people﴾ [Yusuf: 9]

is that when that matter which occupies their minds and takes part of their thinking finds a solution, their minds will be at rest, and their affairs for managing their worldly life will be set right.

Thus we understand that their striving toward righteousness is bound to their desires in life, according to their understanding of righteousness and life.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿A speaker among them said: Do not kill Yusuf, but cast him into the depth of the well; some passing caravan will pick him up, if you are going to act.﴾ [Yusuf: 10]

1 - Al-Naghs: the troubling of life... One says naghsa 'alayhi 'aysahu, meaning he troubled his life; and naghsa 'alayna means he cut off from us what we loved to have more of; and whoever cuts off something of what one loves to increase is a munaghghis. [Lisan al-Arab, root: n-gh-s]

2 - Ghayabat al-jubb: that which is hidden from sight in its sides and conceals what is inside it. God the Exalted says: ﴿...and cast him into the depth of the well...﴾ [Yusuf: 10]. It was also read as ghayabat in the plural [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/65]. The ghayabah of everything is its bottom; and they fell into a ghayabah of the land, i.e., into a low part of it. [Lisan al-Arab, root: gh-y-b]

3 - Al-sayyar: one who travels much; and al-sayyarah is a traveling group of travelers. God the Exalted says: ﴿And a caravan came...﴾ [Yusuf: 19], and His saying: ﴿an enjoyment for you and for the travelers...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 96], i.e., for the travelers. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/340]

Thus we see the lessening of evil when one of them rejects the principle of killing and substitutes concealment by casting him into the well.

God, exalted is He, did not specify for us the name of the speaker, so that He might protect them all from being suspected of wrongdoing.

Al-jubb is the well that is not lined (al-bi'r ghayr al-matwiyy)(1). We know that when people dig a well, its water flows continuously, and a landslide may come and block the well. For this reason, they build around the mouth of the well some bricks to protect it from being filled in. They call such a well a "lined well" (bi'r matwiyy), and thus the water remains in the well in a state of continual flow.

As for the phrase: ﴿ghayabat al-jubb (10)﴾ [Yusuf]

That is: the hidden area of the well, which is usually above the water, and what is in it is hidden from the eyes.

One may ask: how could he be cast into a hidden place, given the words of one of the brothers: ﴿some of the travelers will pick him up (10)﴾ [Yusuf]?

We say: in such a statement there is a lowering of the degree of evil that was blazing in the suggestion of some of them to kill Yusuf; and in this suggestion there is a reduction of the matter of killing or throwing him to the ground.

After that, the speaker(2) returned to his normal state, and the feeling of brotherhood became sound in him, and he said:

﴿if you are going to act (10)﴾ [Yusuf]

That is: he expected that they would not reject his suggestion.

Thus God, exalted is He, explains to us how this matter was settled. The holder of this opinion did not confront his brothers' proposal to kill Yusuf or to throw him on the ground with violence; rather, he began to lure them so that he might draw out from them the fury of anger. So he did not say to them, "Do not kill him," but rather said, "Do not kill Yusuf."

In his pronouncing of the name there is tenderness toward them.

He adds:

﴿and throw him into the hidden part of the well; some of the travelers will pick him up, if you are going to act (10)﴾ [Yusuf]

As if he hoped that they would retreat from their plan.

God, exalted is He, then says:

﴿They said: "O our father, why do you not trust us with Yusuf, when we are indeed his sincere advisers? (11)"﴾

1 - Al-tawa: the well lined with stones; it is said: tawa al-rakiyya tayyan, meaning he lined the well with stones and bricks (Lisan al-Arab, entry: ṭwy).

2 - Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir [4/3452]: "The speaker is Yahudha (Judah), the eldest son of Ya'qub; this was said by Ibn 'Abbas. It is also said: Rubil (Reuben), who was his maternal cousin; and it is also said: Shim'un (Simeon)."

3 - Iltaqata al-shay' wa-laqatahu: he took the thing to safeguard it or for another purpose. A person picks up only what he sees as beneficial. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up (8)﴾ [al-Qasas], so they took him, thinking he would be useful and beneficial to them. Likewise His saying ﴿some of the travelers will pick him up (10)﴾ [Yusuf]: some travelers take him to benefit from him and to safeguard him (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/198).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 12, verse 11:

After they agreed with their brother who had softened the matter of killing and brought it down to the matter of casting him into the well, they began to carry it out. One of them spoke, addressing his father, while all the brothers were present.

﴿O our father, what is [the matter] with you that you do not trust us with Joseph?...(11)﴾ [Yusuf]

Whenever you hear the words of a group, know that one of them was the one who spoke, and the rest affirmed his words, either by silence or by gesture.

To make this clear, read the words of the Truth, glorified is He, about the supplication of Musa, peace be upon him, against Pharaoh, and Harun was with him.

Musa, peace be upon him, said:

﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment (88)﴾ [Yunus]

The Truth, glorified is He, responded to the supplication of Musa:

﴿Your supplication has been answered...(89)﴾ [Yunus]

The one who supplicated was Musa, and the one who affirmed the supplication was Harun, peace be upon him.

Thus we understand that the one who said:

﴿O our father, what is [the matter] with you that you do not trust us with Joseph, while we are indeed his sincere well-wishers (11)﴾ [Yusuf]

these words that occur in the verse we are now reflecting upon, is one of Joseph's brothers, and the rest of the brothers affirmed his words.

Their saying: ﴿What is [the matter] with you that you do not trust us with Joseph, while we are indeed his sincere well-wishers (11)﴾ [Yusuf]

indicates that there had been earlier attempts on their part in this regard, and the father had not agreed with them.

Their saying: ﴿while we are indeed his sincere well-wishers (11)﴾ [Yusuf]

means that they will look after him, and no harm or evil will befall him; they will give him full attention, so there is no need for the father to fear for him.

The presentation of what came from the tongue of Joseph's brothers continues:

﴿Send him with us tomorrow, to enjoy himself and play, and indeed we will surely guard him (12)﴾

Note 1: "tamasa al-shay'": its form changed or its trace was effaced; "tamasahu ghayruhu": he disfigured it or erased and removed it; "tamasa 'aynahu": he blinded it. His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth...(88)﴾ [Yunus] mean: send down upon it what will erase and destroy it [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/406].

Note 2: "shadda al-habl": he tied it firmly, and "shadda asrahu": he strengthened its bond and secured its fetter so that it never escapes, i.e., he tightened control over him. ﴿And We strengthened their captivity...(28)﴾ [al-Insan] means: We secured their bonds and gained control over them. His words ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom...(20)﴾ [Sad] mean: We reinforced it. His words ﴿and harden upon their hearts...(88)﴾ [Yunus] mean: tighten the covering and bind it firmly upon their hearts, and it is a supplication against them. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/344].

Note 3: "rata'a yarta'u": he ate and drank as he wished in abundance and plenty; its origin is the eating of livestock, and it is used figuratively for a human being when he gives free rein to the desires of his belly [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/254].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 12, verse 12:

Because they used to go out for pasturing and work, they had to come up with a pretext so that their father would permit them to take Yusuf out with them. Yusuf was in his childhood, and play is, for him, a beloved and permitted matter, because he is still below the age of obligation (taklif). Play is a permissible activity intended to relax the soul.

The Shari'ah prefers that play be in a field that may be needed in earnest later on, such as a child learning swimming, wrestling, or hitting a target, which is archery(1). Thus we understand the meaning of play: it is an activity that does not distract from a duty. As for lahw (frivolous diversion)(2), it is an activity that distracts from a duty.

There are some games that people play while sitting together, and then the caller to prayer calls the adhan, and conversation carries them away, and they do not pay attention to the iqamah of the prayer at its time. Thus diversion carries them away from what is necessary. But if they paid attention to the iqamah of the prayer, the matter would be merely a harmless entertainment.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿He said, "Indeed, it grieves me that you take him away, and I fear that the wolf will devour him while you are heedless of him." (13)﴾

1 - On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: (The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by a group who were shooting arrows, and said: "Shoot, O sons of Isma'il, for your father was an archer.") Narrated by Ahmad in Musnad [1/264], and al-Bukhari in his Sahih [2899] from Salamah ibn al-Akwa', may Allah be pleased with him, with similar wording.

2 - Lahiya yalhu lahwan: he entertained himself and occupied himself with what gives him pleasure and delight, or amused himself with what benefits him not. Allah the Most High said: ﴿But that which is with Allah is better than diversion and trade...(11)﴾ [al-Jumu'ah]. Lahw here means singing, drums, and flutes that accompanied the return of merchants at the time of prayer. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/205].

Al-Sha'rawi's words here: the father's speech must have angered them, for it is evidence of his exceptional love, to the degree that he fears separation from Yusuf because of his inability to be patient without him, and his intense care for him. Then he brought them the other statement, which is:

﴿And I fear that the wolf may devour him while you are heedless of him.﴾ [Yusuf 12:13]

Some people said: Ya'qub taught them to lie; had it not been for that, they would not have known how to tell this lie.

We note that Ya'qub gave the brothers a glance (of consideration): he did not say, "I fear that the wolf may devour him while you are sitting," but rather said:

﴿And I fear that the wolf may devour him while you are heedless of him.﴾ [Yusuf 12:13]

This is to educate them in the sentiments of brotherhood, which require that they not treat their brother with harm, nor let anyone else treat him with harm, except when they are heedless of their brother.

Note also in their reply their inability to answer his saying:

﴿Indeed, it grieves me that you take him away..﴾ [Yusuf 12:13]

This love of Ya'qub for Yusuf is what drove them to resentment toward Yusuf, and they only responded to his fear that the wolf would devour him. The Qur'an brought what they said:

﴿They said, "If the wolf devours him while we are a group, then indeed we would be losers."﴾ [Yusuf 12:14]

1 - Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir [2/470]: "They took this word from his mouth and made it their excuse for what they did." Al-Suyuti, in "al-Durr al-Manthur" [4/510], cited reports on this matter, saying: Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Sulafi in al-Tuyuriyyat reported from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not prompt people, for they will lie. The sons of Ya'qub did not know that a wolf eats people; when their father prompted them, they lied and said, 'A wolf ate him.'"

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, reveals to us their attempts to reassure their father, so that he would permit Yusuf to go out with them. For this reason they expressed their disbelief that the wolf should devour him while they were a band around him, and they declared that if that happened they would lose their dignity before themselves and before their people, and they would not accept this humiliation for themselves.(١)

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿So when they took him away and agreed to put him in the depths of the well, and We revealed to him: "You will surely inform them of this their affair while they do not perceive."﴾ (15)

1 - Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir [4/3462]: "His words ﴿Indeed, we would then be losers (14)﴾ [Yusuf] mean: indeed we would be losers in guarding our flocks, that is, if we cannot repel the wolf from our brother, then we are even less able to repel it from our flocks."..
2 - Jama'a amrahu (جمع أمره): he resolved upon it or made it firm. Allah says: ﴿Then Pharaoh withdrew and gathered his plot, then came (60)﴾ [Ta-Ha], meaning he resolved upon it and made it firm. And ajma'a al-qawm 'ala amr (أجمع القوم على أمر) means the people agreed upon a matter; and ajma'a al-amr (أجمع الأمر) means he resolved upon it and made it firm. Allah says: ﴿So gather your plot, then come in ranks (64)﴾ [Ta-Ha]. And Allah says: ﴿And they agreed to put him in the depths of the well (15)﴾ [Yusuf], meaning they agreed. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/127]..

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 12, verse 15:

﴿So when they took him away and agreed (1) to put him in the depths of the well, We revealed to him: "You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs while they do not perceive."﴾ (15)

His saying, the Truth:

﴿And they agreed to put him in the depths of the well...﴾ (15) [Yusuf]

It shows us that this matter was subject to discussion among them, with back-and-forth, until they settled upon it (2).

Allah, the Truth, the Glorified, inspired Yusuf, peace be upon him, with what they would do. Revelation (wahy), as we know, is an informing in secrecy.

It will come in the story that Yusuf, peace be upon him, after he assumed the office of vizier in Egypt, and they entered upon him, took a drinking cup, struck it with his fingers, and said to them: "Listen to what the cup says; it says: You have a brother, and you did such and such to him" (3).

Some of the exegetes said: Allah, the Glorified, revealed to him, and his brothers did not notice this revelation.

We say: Revelation is an informing in secrecy, and it cannot be perceived by anyone other than the one to whom it is revealed. On that basis, we see that they did not know this matter until after Yusuf had taken the reins of the vizierate in Egypt; indeed, they did not even recognize that Yusuf was their brother, because they said to him at that moment:

﴿If he steals, a brother of his stole before (4)...﴾ (77) [Yusuf]

The meaning of revelation in this verse, about which we are reflecting, is the comforting of the wild creature (iynas al-wahsh). It is a divine inspiration (warid) that the satanic inspiration (warid al-shaytan) cannot repel. Inspiration (ilham) is an inspiration for those who are not prophets, just as we clarified in the matter that happened with the mother of Musa when Allah revealed to her to cast him into the river (5).

A divine inspiration meets no opposition in the human soul. Allah revealed to Yusuf what would comfort his loneliness (6) when his brothers threw him into the well, where he was far from his father's tenderness and his companionship with his brother, and his separation from his homeland in which he had grown up (7) and from the environment to which he was accustomed.

So it was necessary that the heavens give him a sign that what had happened to him was not a rejection of you, O Yusuf; rather, it was a preparation for you to face a matter more important than what you were in. And that your creditors, who are your brothers, would be compelled one day to knock on your door seeking your help, asking you for their provisions, and you would recognize them while they would not recognize you.

This is concerning Yusuf's side. As for the well into which they threw him, what remains is for the story to address the matter of the brothers with the father. Allah, the Glorified, then says:

﴿And they came to their father in the evening, weeping.﴾ (16)

Notes:

1 - Jama'a amrahu: he resolved upon it or firmed it up. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then Pharaoh withdrew and gathered his plot, then came (60)﴾ [Ta-Ha], meaning he resolved upon it and firmed it up. And ajma'a al-qawm 'ala amr: the people agreed upon a matter; ajma'a al-amr: he resolved upon it and firmed it up. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So gather your plot, then come in ranks...(64)﴾ [Ta-Ha], and He says: ﴿And they agreed to put him in the depths of the well...(15)﴾ [Yusuf], meaning: they agreed. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/127].

2 - al-Qurtubi mentioned in this that when Ya'qub, peace be upon him, sent him with them, he took from them a solemn covenant to guard him, and handed him over to Rubil, and said: "O Rubil, he is young, and you know, my son, my compassion for him. If he is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink; if he is weary, carry him; then hasten to return him to me." He said: So they took him, carrying him on their shoulders; no one would put him down but another would lift him [see: Tafsir al-Qurtubi 4/3462].

3 - Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "When the brothers of Yusuf entered upon Yusuf, he recognized them while they did not recognize him. The cup was brought, and he placed it on his hand, then struck it, so it resonated, and he said: Indeed this cup informs me that you had a brother from your father called Yusuf, who follows your religion, and that you took him away and cast him into the depths of the well, then you came to your father and said: The wolf has eaten him, and you brought his shirt with false blood. Then some of them said to others: Indeed this cup is informing him of your news." [cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 4/511].

4 - They mean Yusuf, peace be upon him. Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Qatadah: Yusuf, peace be upon him, had stolen an idol of his maternal grandfather and broke it. Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid, who said: The first affliction that befell Yusuf, as it has reached me, was that his paternal aunt, daughter of Ishaq, who was the eldest child of Ishaq, had Ishaq's girdle with her, and they would inherit it by seniority; whoever possessed it among those in her care would have authority over it, to do with him as he pleased. When Ya'qub had a son, Yusuf, his aunt had nursed him, and she had a special affection for him and he for her; she loved no one as she loved him. When he grew up and reached years of age, Ya'qub's soul yearned for him, so he came to her and said: "O my sister, hand Yusuf over to me, for by Allah I cannot bear that he be away from me for an hour." She said: "By Allah, I will not leave him." Then she said: "Leave him with me for some days; I will look at him and be consoled about him, perhaps that will console me for him," or as she said. When Ya'qub left her, she took Ishaq's girdle and tied it on Yusuf under his garments. Then she said: "Ishaq's girdle has been lost; look for who took it and who has it." It was sought, then she said: "Search the household," and they searched them, and found it with Yusuf. She said: "By Allah, he is mine as a slave; I will do with him what I please." Ya'qub came to her and she told him the news. He said to her: "You and that; if he did this, then he is your slave; I cannot do otherwise." So she held him, and Ya'qub could not get him back until she died [see Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/486].

5 - He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿When We revealed to your mother what is revealed (38), that you cast him into the chest, then cast him into the river, and the river will throw him onto the bank...(39)﴾ [Ta-Ha].

6 - Among what has been related about this is what al-Qurtubi transmitted in his tafsir [4/3465]: "al-Dahhak said: Jibril, peace be upon him, descended upon Yusuf while he was in the well and said to him: Shall I teach you words which, if you say them, Allah will hasten your release from this well? He said: Yes. Say: O Creator of every created thing, O Mender of every broken bone, O Witness of every secret conversation, O Present at every gathering, O Reliever of every distress, O Companion of every stranger, O Comforter of every lonely one, bring me relief and hope, and cast your hope into my heart until I hope for no one other than You."
Yusuf repeated them through the night many times, and Allah brought him out of the well on the morning of that day."

7 - It is said of a child when he begins to move and take up motion: darraja; and the old man and the child "yadrij" (crawl/toddle), so he is "darij": walking slowly and feebly, crawling. [Lisan al-Arab, root: d-r-j].

Here, the precision of the Qur'an's expression becomes apparent, expressing the emotions that exist in the human soul. Behold: brothers who deceived their father, plotted against their brother, took him and threw him into the well, though they knew that their father loved him, and was too protective (ḍanīn) to entrust him to them. How will they face this father?

This is the psychological emotion that no natural disposition can sustain. So they said: we will postpone the meeting with our father until evening (ʿishāʾ). Evening is the place of darkness, and it is a cover for the emotions that appear on the faces in the form of agitation, and for the contradiction of the lie of their tongues, because they will not inform the father of the reality that happened, but rather with a fabricated story (mukhtalaq)(2).

Their movements may betray them, their stammering may expose them, and their false features may be revealed before their father. So they said: the night is more concealing for the face than the day, and more veiling of scandals; and when we enter upon our father in the evening, our emotions will not expose us.

Thus they chose the time frame in which they could hide from their deeds:

﴿And they came to their father in the evening, weeping (16)﴾ [Yusuf]

Weeping is a natural, instinctive, innate emotion; a person has no choice in it. Whoever wishes to feign it is pretending to weep, by rubbing his eyes, or bringing some of his saliva and placing it near his eyes, and this is not concealed except when the light is dim. Therefore they came to their father in the evening, performing weeping (3).

When the Almighty spoke about the attributes that He gave to His own Self and gave to none of His creation, He informed us that He is the One who causes death and gives life, and He is the One who makes laugh and makes weep.

The Almighty Himself says:

﴿And that He it is who makes laugh and makes weep (43), and that He it is who causes death and gives life (44)﴾ [al-Najm]

There is no difference between the laughter or weeping of an English person and an Arab; and there is no difference between the death or birth of a Chinese person and an Arab or a Frenchman; these are characteristics shared by all humanity.

If a person feigns laughter, he is pretending to laugh (yatadāḥak); and if a person feigns weeping, he is pretending to weep (yatabākā); that is, he fabricates laughter or weeping, and what exposes all of that is the day.

History carries to us many stories of taking the night as a cover for situations. The best example is Sayyidunā al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with him and content him, when the Battle of Karbala came, and he saw the enemies surrounding him, and he saw the people who had dispersed from him after they had invited him to pledge allegiance, and only a few remained with him; his own soul was dear to him, and it was hard for him that these should be killed in an unequal battle which he himself insisted on entering.

When the night came, he called his companions and said to them:

"If you have been ashamed to flee from me by day, the night has come and has concealed you, so whoever wishes, let him go and leave me" (4).

1 - ḍanantu bi'l-shayʾ aḍunnu: I withheld it, was stingy with it; and he is ḍanīn with it, and a man ḍanīn is a miser. Ḍanna and ḍann mean withholding and stinginess. The Almighty said: ﴿And he is not stingy with the unseen (24)﴾ [al-Takwir], so he does not conceal any unseen matter from the Messenger of Allah, but conveys everything Allah revealed to him of news from the heavens. [See Lisan al-ʿArab, and al-Qamus al-Qawim].
2 - Khalaqa al-kadhib wa'l-ifk yakhluquhu, takhalluquhu, ikhtalaqahu, iftarāhu: he invented it. Al-ikhtilāq: lying, and it is an iftiʿāl from creation and innovation, as if the liar fashioned his speech. [Lisan al-ʿArab, root kh-l-q].
3 - Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir [4/3466]: "Our scholars said: this verse is evidence that a person's weeping does not indicate the truth of his speech, since it may be feigned; some people are able to do that, and some are not. It has been said: feigned tears do not remain hidden, as a wise man said:
When tears intermingle on cheeks, one can tell who wept from who feigned."
4 - Ibn Kathir mentioned in [al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya 8/178] that al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said to his companions: "Whoever loves to return to his family this night, I have given him permission, for these people only want me. This night has covered you, so take it as a veil; let each of you take the hand of a man from my household, then go off across the vast earth in the darkness of this night to your lands and cities, for these people only want me. If they reach me, they will be distracted from seeking anyone else. So go, until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings relief."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 12, verse 17:

The Truthful One, glory be to Him, relates what they said the moment they entered upon their father.

﴿They said: "O our father, we went off racing one another (1), and we left Joseph by our belongings, and the wolf devoured him. But you will not believe us, even though we are truthful."﴾ (12:17)

Word: ﴿nastabiq...﴾ (12:17) [Yusuf]

It expresses the demonstration of one thing's superiority over another in some movement, so that we see who will outpace the other. When two people race in running, we see which of them outpaces the other; this is al-istibaq (racing).

Racing may also take place with an instrument: a person holds a rifle and aims it at a target, and another comes, holds another rifle and tries to hit the target. Whichever of them hits the target first is the superior in this field.

Racing may also take place in archery. We know the shape of the arrow: it is a flexible branch that bends without breaking, with a string fixed to it. The arrow is placed at the middle of the string, the archer draws it, and the arrow is released toward the target.

The accuracy of hitting the target is measured by the strength of the arrow and the power of the shot, and this is called "defining the target."

As for when the contest is in terms of the length of the distance the arrow covers, this is to measure the strength of the archer.

Thus we find that racing has many fields, and all of that is permissible. They were the tribes and sons of Ya'qub, and there is no objection to a person playing a game that does not distract him from his duty, and that may benefit him in whatever matters he encounters. If he meets an enemy, training in the use of the arrow, the spear, or any weapon of combat benefits him. Play that does not divert from obedience and that benefits in time of seriousness is permissible play.

There are games whose purpose people may not perceive, such as football.

I say: there may be two enemies with a time bomb between them, and each side tries to move it away from its position; strength and wisdom appear in each team's attempt to move the ball away from its goal.

But ball games must not distract from duty. For example, when the muezzin calls to prayer, our duty is not to neglect the prayer and continue playing, and the players must take care not to wear clothing that reveals their private parts.

The sons of Ya'qub said:

﴿and we left Joseph by our belongings (3)...﴾ (12:17)

In this there is a breach of the conditions of the agreement with the father, who had permitted Joseph's departure after they had said:

﴿Send him with us tomorrow, he will enjoy himself and play...﴾ (12:12)

And they said:

﴿and indeed we are sincere advisers to him﴾ (12:11)

And they said:

﴿and indeed we are his guardians﴾ (12:12)

So did you take him with you so that he might enjoy himself and play, and eat of the fruits of the trees and the produce, and you would guard him, or to guard your belongings while you race one another?

Thus this was the first of the lies they told, and this was the first violation of the condition of his father's permission for him to go out with them. And because "the suspicious one almost says, 'Take me'," we find them saying:

﴿So the wolf devoured him. But you will not believe us, even though we are truthful.﴾ (12:17)

Or: they said that because they knew their father would not believe them no matter what they said. We know that "āmana" either takes its object directly, as in "Allah granted him security from hunger," or in His word, the Truth:

﴿and He gave them security from fear﴾ (106:4)

Or it takes the preposition bi, and one says "āmana bihi," meaning he affirmed and believed in it.

Or one says "āmana lahu," meaning he affirmed what he said.

Here they accuse their father of being a liar toward them, even if they were truthful, while they knew they were not truthful; but they brought the word of truth to conceal their lie.

Then the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says after that:

﴿And they came upon his shirt with false blood (4)... He said: "Rather, your souls have embellished a matter for you (5). So patience is beautiful, and Allah is the one sought for help against what you describe."﴾ (12:18)

1 - istabaqa: they competed so that each would outpace the other. istabaqa al-shay': they competed in running toward it to reach it. ﴿They said: "O our father, we went off racing one another"﴾ (12:17), i.e., we compete in running and outpacing. ﴿And they both raced to the door﴾ (12:25), each tried to reach it before the other. And He, exalted, says: ﴿So race to the good deeds﴾ (2:148), compete to reach them or to do them before others [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/302].

2 - Play may be praiseworthy if it does not conflict with virtuous values; but if play diverts a person from duties, it is blameworthy, and frivolity is never anything but blameworthy.

3 - al-mata': applies to much and little, as a verbal noun, and is pluralized as amti'a with respect to what one benefits from and enjoys. He, exalted, says: ﴿seeking ornaments or goods﴾ (13:17), i.e., making things from which one benefits. And He, exalted, says: ﴿Those who disbelieved wish that you were negligent of your weapons and your goods﴾ (4:102), the plural of mata' meaning things one benefits from, such as food, tools of war, property, and the like [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/215].

4 - al-qamis: what surrounds the body; it may be called shi'ar, and what is above it is dithar. Every garment may be called qamis; its plurals are aqmisa, qumus and qumsan [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/133].

5 - Mujahid said: it was the blood of a kid or young goat that they had slaughtered. Qatada said: it was the blood of a gazelle. That is, they came upon his shirt with blood that was falsely attributed to him. Al-Hasan and 'A'isha read "bi-damin kadhib" with an unpointed dal, meaning fresh blood, and it is related that it is the changed blood, as al-Sha'bi said [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 4/3471].

6 - sawwalat nafsuhu lahu amran: she made a matter appealing to him so that he would do it; and sawwala lahu al-shaytan: he was misled by it. Al-taswil is making a thing seem good, adorning it, and making it beloved to a person so that he does or says it [Lisan al-Arab, root s-w-l].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (*Tafsir al-Sha'rawi*, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 12, verse 18:

It is as if Joseph's shirt was with them. It is said that Ya'qub (Jacob) remarked, concerning the shirt that came with the false blood, that the wolf must have been merciful: it ate Yusuf's flesh but did not tear his shirt. It seems he already knew that there was a plot which God would reveal to him.(١)

Some scholars describe the story of Joseph by way of the shirt:

Here his brothers came with his shirt, stained with false blood.

In the middle of the surah(٢) comes the matter of Joseph's shirt, whether it was torn from behind at the moment the wife of the chief (al-'Aziz) seized him, seeking to seduce him(٣) from himself.

At the end of the surah(٤), his brothers send his shirt to his father, and his father's sight returns.

For this reason, scholars and men of letters have taken the word "shirt" as a symbol for certain things. The well-known example is what people say about the conflict between 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and Mu'awiya, may Allah be pleased with him: Mu'awiya held up the shirt of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, demanding vengeance from 'Ali, so it was said "the shirt of 'Uthman" as a symbol for concealing the aim from watchful eyes. Mu'awiya's aim was to rule in place of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And they came upon his shirt with false blood.. (18)﴾ [Yusuf]

It is as if the shirt was with them, and they smeared upon it blood that was a lie, because blood does not lie; rather, it was the one who brought the blood of a sheep and put it on the shirt who lied.

The Truth, glory be to Him, chose here to give the description in the form of a verbal noun (*masdar*) for emphasis, as if the blood itself were the one that lied. Just as you say "so-and-so is just" (*'adil*), and you may describe a person by saying "so-and-so is justice" ('adl), meaning that justice has become embodied in him; or you may say "so-and-so is evil" (*dhu sharr*), and another replies, "rather, he is evil itself." This is an intensification of the act.

Could the blood have been described as truthful blood?

We say: yes, had the wolf actually eaten Yusuf; and Yusuf's shirt had been stained with Yusuf's blood and torn. But that did not happen. Rather, the lie almost shouts out in that event, saying, "I am a lie."

For if the wolf had truly eaten him, the blood would have seeped from inside the shirt to the outside; but they brought the blood of a sheep and smeared the shirt with it from the outside.

By God, if the wolf had indeed eaten him, would not its fangs have torn the shirt?

When their deception was exposed before their father, one of them secretly signalled to the others and whispered to them: "Say to your father: 'Robbers came upon him and killed him.'" Ya'qub overheard the whisper and said: "The robbers have more need of his shirt than of his blood."(٦) This is what the books of biography (*sira*) say.

This confirms Ya'qub's insight (*firasa*),(٧) the insight that any investigator in a murder case must possess, when he turns his questions over to the accused and to the witnesses; for the investigator knows that the liar will not draw his statements from reality, but from a disturbed imagination.

For this reason it is said: "If you are a liar, then be a man of good memory."(٨)

Here the Truth brings what came from the tongue of Ya'qub:

﴿Rather, your own selves have made a matter seem fine to you. So patience is fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe. (18)﴾ [Yusuf]

"As-sawl" (السول): it is relaxation, because when a person's nerves are tense, he wants to loosen up, so he rests a little, and afterwards he finds in himself some ease in his body and his pulse.

We take ﴿sawwalat (سولت).. (18)﴾ [Yusuf]: this means "made easy and smoothed," and since your own selves have made this matter seem fine to you, I will receive it with what is fitting for this situation, which is patience.

﴿So patience is fitting.. (18)﴾ [Yusuf]

Those who try to catch an error in the Qur'an say: "Can patience be 'fitting' (*jamil*)?"

We say: they do not know that patience is spoken of with "be patient for such-and-such" (*isbir 'an kadha*) when the matter concerns a desire that may bring pain, as one says "be patient away from wine," "be patient away from gambling," or "be patient away from usury."

And one says "be patient in such-and-such" (*isbir 'ala kadha*) when patience involves pain for you; and patience is fitting when there is no complaint or distress in it.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

﴿And forsake them with fitting forsaking. (10)﴾ [al-Muzzammil]

Those who search for contradiction or conflict in the Qur'an are simply people who do not know how to receive it and understand it. Ya'qub, peace be upon him, has made clear to us that fitting patience is the patience in which there is no complaint, and he is the one who said:

﴿I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah.. (86)﴾ [Yusuf]

Thus we know there is a difference between complaining to the Lord and complaining about the decree of the Lord.

For this reason Ya'qub, peace be upon him, says here:

﴿So patience is fitting.. (18)﴾ [Yusuf]

And it is followed by:

﴿And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe. (18)﴾ [Yusuf]

It is as if fitting patience is a difficult matter for the human soul, and Ya'qub was not able to believe what his sons told him; how could he believe a lie? And how could he confront his sons with what they had done? They were also his sons; yet he was unable to expose their lie to them.

An example of this is what is found in the Arab heritage, when it was said to a man: "Your son has killed your brother." He said:

I say to myself, consoling and comforting it: one of my hands has been struck, and it did not refuse.

Both are compensations for the loss of their companion: this is my brother when I call him, and that is my son.

Such situations are hard and require compassion, because the one who passes through them is torn between a matter that demands severity and a situation that demands mercy; how can a person combine the two?

It is a matter that is grievous for God's creatures, and a person must inevitably turn to God in it. For this reason, we have been taught by him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that when a matter distresses him, he stood up to pray.(١١) "Distressed" (*hazaba*) by a matter means that confronting it exceeds a person's capacities, so he resorts to the highest Cause; and for this reason Ya'qub, peace be upon him, said:

﴿And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe. (18)﴾ [Yusuf]

His words "what you describe" (*taslifun*) mean that you are not telling the truth, but describing something that does not correspond to reality, as in the words of the Exalted:

﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe as falsehood, "This is lawful and this is unlawful." (116)﴾ [al-Nahl]

That is, your tongues themselves describe the speech as a lie.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe. (180)﴾ [al-Saffat]

It means that those who said what was reported as a description have lied in what they said, and the outcome of their lie was exposed.

﴿So patience is fitting. And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe. (18)﴾ [Yusuf]

Thus Ya'qub, peace be upon him, expressed himself: the limbs may be still, but the heart may be crowded with worries and lack tranquillity; therefore one must seek help from Allah.

The Truth, glory be to Him, has taught us to say in the Opening of the Book:

﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help. (5)﴾ [al-Fatihah]

You stand to worship Allah and before Him; but worldly concerns may distract you from worship even during the act of worship itself. Therefore you seek help from your Creator so that you may be sincere in your worship.

After the Truth, glory be to Him, presented the father's position with his sons, we come to the position of Yusuf, peace be upon him, in the well.

He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿A caravan came, and they sent their water-drawer, and he let down his bucket. He said: "Good news! This is a boy!" And they concealed him as merchandise. And Allah knows well what they do. (19)﴾

1 - Al-Qurtubi, in his *Tafsir* [4/3471], reported: "When Ya'qub, peace be upon him, examined the shirt and found no tear in it and no mark, he inferred from that that they were lying, and he said to them: 'When has this wolf been so judicious that it eats Yusuf and does not tear the shirt?'" This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and others.
2 - This is in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿She said: "It was she who sought to seduce me from myself," and a witness from her household testified: "If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth and he is among the liars. But if his shirt is torn from behind, then she has lied and he is among the truthful." (26–27)﴾ [Yusuf].
3 - *Rawada 'ala al-shay'* (راود على الشيء): to seek it from someone with effort, cunning and bargaining. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him from himself.. (23)﴾ [Yusuf], meaning that she sought him from himself through attempts and deception. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/281, adapted].
4 - This is in His saying, the Exalted, concerning Yusuf, peace be upon him, when he said to his brothers: ﴿Take this shirt of mine and cast it upon the face of my father; he will regain his sight.. (93)﴾ [Yusuf].
5 - This is the style of rhetorical inimitability (*i'jaz*), and it contains an allusion to a fabricated matter.
6 - Al-Qurtubi, in his *Tafsir* [4/3472], mentions the attempts of Ya'qub's sons to justify what happened, and the exposure of their affair before their father through his insight. He said: "It is reported that they said to him: 'Rather, robbers killed him.' Their statements differed, so he suspected them. Ya'qub said to them: 'You claim that the wolf ate him; but if it had eaten him, it would have torn his shirt before reaching his skin, and I see no tear in the shirt. You claim that robbers killed him; but if they had killed him, they would have taken his shirt. Do they want anything but his clothes?'"
7 - *Firasa* (الفراسة): regarding looking, observing carefully, reflecting upon a thing and perceiving it. It has two meanings, as stated by Ibn al-Athir:
One: what God places in the hearts of His friends (*awliya'*), so that they know the states of some people through a kind of wonderworking (*karamat*), correct assumption and intuition.
The second: a kind that is learned through evidences, experiences, temperaments and characters, by which the states of people are known. Cited by Ibn Manzur in *Lisan al-'Arab*, root *f-r-s*.
8 - *Dhikr* (الذكر): memory of a thing, remembering it; *rajul dhakir* means a man of good memory and retention; *dhikr* and *dhikra* are the opposite of forgetting; *tadhakkur* is recalling what you had forgotten. [Lisan al-'Arab, root *dh-k-r*].
9 - *Hajarahu yahjuruhu hajran wa hijranan*: he abandoned him with displeasure and aversion. The Exalted says: ﴿And the abomination, forsake (5)﴾ [al-Muddaththir], meaning: abandon the abomination entirely, shunning it and hating it. This command, with respect to the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, means: persevere in abandoning it, for he never committed any abomination. The Exalted's saying ﴿and forsake them with fitting forsaking (10)﴾ [al-Muzzammil] means: leave them and keep away from them with forbearance, without harming them. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/298].
10 - Fitting patience is patience together with contentment and entrusting the matter to the One who holds it. From the concept of the Imam's insights (*khawatir al-Imam*).
11 - From Hudhayfah, who said: "The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, whenever a matter distressed him, would pray." Recorded by Imam Ahmad in his *Musnad* [5/388] and Abu Dawud in his *Sunan* [1319].
12 - *Wasf al-amr* (وصف الأمر): mentioning it, knowing it and speaking of it. The Exalted says: ﴿Your tongues describe (taṣifu) the lie (116)﴾ [al-Nahl], meaning: you mention it and say it. The Exalted also says: ﴿Glory be to Him and exalted is He above what they describe (100)﴾ [al-An'am], meaning: above the description they ascribe to Him, which does not befit His perfection, such as having a partner or a son or other things. And He says: ﴿He will repay them for their description (139)﴾ [al-An'am], meaning: the recompense for their description and His punishment of it. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/339].
13 - *Jamal* (الجمال): radiance and beauty, which may be attributed to the sensible and the immaterial. The Exalted says: ﴿So patience is fitting (18)﴾ [Yusuf], which is immaterial beauty; and His saying: ﴿So forgive with fitting forgiveness (85)﴾ [al-Hijr], which carries no blame or reproach; and *sarah jamil* (fitting release) means divorce accompanied by kindness to the divorced woman, granting her rights in full and without harm; and His saying: ﴿and forsake them with fitting forsaking (10)﴾ [al-Muzzammil], in which there is no harm by word or deed. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/128].
14 - *Sayyara* (السيارة): a travelling, journeying group. The Exalted says: ﴿And a caravan came (19)﴾ [Yusuf], meaning a travelling group; and His saying: ﴿a provision for you and for the travellers (96)﴾ [al-Ma'idah], meaning for travellers. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/340].
15 - *Warada al-ma'* (ورد الماء): you came to the water in order to drink. *Al-wird* is the water to which one comes; *al-warida* is the water-carrier; and *al-wird* is the one who comes, namely those who come to the water. [Lisan al-'Arab, root *w-r-d*]. *Warada al-ma'*: he aimed at it, reached it and arrived at it.
16 - *Dalw* (الدلو): the vessel that draws water from a well or the like. The Exalted says: ﴿So they sent their water-drawer and he let down his bucket (19)﴾ [Yusuf], meaning he lowered it into the well to bring up water from it. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/231].
17 - Al-Qurtubi said in his *Tafsir* [4/3475]: "Regarding its meaning there are two opinions:
One: it is the name of the boy.
Two: 'O good news! This is your time and your moment.' Qatadah said: he gave good news to his companions that he had found a slave. Al-Suddi said: he called a man named Bushra. Al-Nahhas said: Qatadah's view is preferable, because no name is mentioned in the Qur'an except rarely. Al-Qurtubi said: this is more correct, because if it were a proper name it would not be attached to the pronoun of the speaker."
18 - *Asarartu al-amr wa al-hadith*: I concealed it. *Asarra ilayhi al-hadith*: he told him the matter secretly, without anyone else with him knowing of it. The Exalted says: ﴿and they concealed the regret (54)﴾ [Yunus], meaning they hid it in their breasts and their inner selves. And His saying in the story of Yusuf: ﴿and they concealed him as merchandise (19)﴾ [Yusuf], meaning they hid him. And His saying: ﴿you send them tidings of affection (1)﴾ [al-Mumtahanah], meaning they convey to them news of the Muslims and their affairs because of the affection between you; this is a rebuke and reproach for whoever does this. Or it means you conceal affection for them, that is, you make your affection for them secret, hiding it from the Muslims out of hypocrisy and deceit. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/310].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 12, verse 19:

And the Exalted did not say: from where did the caravan (sayyarah) come? Or to where are they heading?

What is meant by the sayyarah (caravan) are the people who make travel their profession, such as those who used to journey in the winter and summer journeys, for the purpose of trade and bringing goods.

The caravan would not move with all its members to the well; rather, one of them would go to the well to bring water for them, and he is called the wārid (water-fetcher). This wārid went to the well to fetch water for the rest of the caravan, and he lowered his bucket into the well; the rope of the bucket is called the risha' (rope).

When the bucket descended to the level of Yusuf, peace be upon him, Yusuf clung to the rope. The wārid felt the weight of what the rope carried, and he looked down, and found a boy clinging to the bucket, so he called out:

﴿O good news! This is a boy!﴾ [Yusuf: 19]

That is: he is saying, "O good news! This is your time," as if he is announcing something good to his people; for the bucket had brought up not only water, but also a boy.

The Exalted says:

﴿And they concealed him as merchandise.﴾ [Yusuf: 19]

That is: they hid him and treated him as if he were merchandise, and did not let him walk beside them, fearing that he might be a runaway slave (ābiq)(1) whose master would search for him, and they wanted to sell him.

The Exalted concludes the verse with His saying:

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing of what they do.﴾ [Yusuf: 19]

This statement refers back to those who concealed him as merchandise, namely those who displayed him for sale. Then the Exalted says:

﴿And they sold him for a paltry price, a few dirhams counted; and they were of those who were indifferent to him.﴾ [Yusuf: 20]

1 – abaqa, ya'biqu: he fled from his owner. The Exalted said: ﴿When he fled to the laden ship﴾ [al-Saffat: 140]; the leaving of his people by Yunus, peace be upon him, was considered an flight (ibaq) because he was a servant belonging to Allah and to the message which Allah had commanded him to carry out. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/4].

2 – bakhasa, yabkhasu (bakhsan): he withheld his due from him, diminishing it and not paying it in full. The Exalted said: ﴿And do not diminish people's goods﴾ [al-A'raf: 85]. The paltry price (thaman bakhs) is a small price that falls short of its equivalent: ﴿And they sold him for a paltry price﴾ [Yusuf: 20]. And His saying: ﴿So he fears neither diminution nor oppression﴾ [al-Jinn: 13], meaning: he does not fear loss or injustice. [al-Qamus al-Qawim: 1/56].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 12, verse 20:

We know that they did not buy him; rather they came upon him (ʿathara ʿalayhi). We also know that the word "shira'" (purchase) indicates a sale too, i.e., they sold him for a paltry price (thaman bakhs); that is, for a meagre price (thaman zahid), and slaves in those days were valued in money.

Al-bakhs (paltry) means deficiency (al-nuqs), and it may be in quantity or in quality. So it may be worth, for example, a hundred dirhams, while they sold him for only twenty dirhams. The slave in Joseph's time was valued in currency, and they sold him for a paltry sum, at a price lower in value, either in quantity or in quality.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, wished to make the matter clearer, so He said:

﴿And they sold him for a small price, a few dirhams, and they were of those who were indifferent to him (20)﴾ [Yusuf]

Al-zuhd (indifference) is precisely the reason for the paltry price: they feared that his father or his companion would search for him. It is as if they said to themselves: whatever comes of him will be a gain for us.(1)

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife: "Honour his residence (mathwahu), perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son." Thus did We establish Joseph in the land, and that We might teach him the interpretation of events. And Allah is dominant over His affair, but most people do not know (21)﴾
