An example of this is what happened to the Shah of Iran: he had sovereignty, had every means of civilization, and had a strong army at his command; then the Truthful One willed to remove sovereignty from him, and others undid the invisible bolts with which the Shah had fastened his throne, and so sovereignty departed from him.

In this world you hold control over your limbs: you say to the hand, "Strike so-and-so," and your hand strikes so-and-so. But when the Last Day comes, a person does not hold control over his limbs, because sovereignty on that day belongs to Allah alone; glorified is He who said: ﴿..."To whom belongs sovereignty today?" "To Allah, the One, the Subduer."﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. On the Last Day all authorities cease, and authority belongs to Allah alone. Alongside "al-mulk" and "al-milk" there is also al-malakut, which is what you do not see with the instruments of the senses. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the realm (malakut) of the heavens and the earth...﴾ [Al-An'am: 75]

That is: the Truthful One, glorified is He, revealed to Abraham the hidden secrets of the created world; and you see scientists tracing the secrets of the kingdoms of plants and animals, and you marvel at the precision of Allah's creation.

Whoever Allah grants the precision of knowledge and the insight of scholars sees, through the radiance of sight and knowledge, the world of malakut, extracts secrets, and deduces truths.

Yusuf, peace be upon him, adds in his supplication to his Lord: ﴿And You have taught me of the interpretation of dreams (ta'wil al-ahadith)...﴾ [Yusuf: 101]

He acknowledges Allah's favour upon him in singling him out with the ability to interpret ahadith (events, narrations, dreams); those by which he interpreted the dreams of the two young men who were with him in prison, and interpreted the dream of the king; this interpretation led him to rule, and this is not strange or wondrous with respect to the power of Allah, glorified is He.

Yusuf says, giving thanks to Allah: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth...﴾ [Yusuf: 101]

Since He, glorified is He, is the Creator of everything, it is not strange that He teaches whomever He wills; as though Yusuf's faith had brought him to know what the Truthful One said: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾ [Al-Mulk: 14]

In our lives we find that the one who made a device, which others use, explains the specifications of using the device or tool, even if it is a threshing-sledge or a plough, in order to ensure for the device the proper movement by which it performs its work.

If one of us has a car that breaks down, he summons the mechanic to look at what is wrong with it; if the mechanic is trustworthy, he precisely diagnoses what the car needs and repairs it; but if he is untrustworthy, you will find him spoiling what is sound and increasing work the car does not need. Thus we see that every craftsman in his field knows the secrets of his craft; how much more, then, the Supreme Creator, glorified and exalted is He? He is All-Aware and All-Knowing of everything.

Why did Yusuf say of the Truthful One: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth...﴾ [Yusuf: 101]? Because he knows that the Truthful One created man; and man has a beginning and an end, which no one knows except Allah, glorified is He. A man may die when his age is a day, or die in his mother's womb, or after a hundred years, and changes pass over a person.

As for the heavens and the earth, they are stable creations: the sun does not need a spare part, it has not fallen, and it gives warmth to the earth; and it is raised above the earth, not falling upon it, by the will of Allah.

The Truthful One says: ﴿...And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission. Indeed, Allah is, toward mankind, Kind and Merciful.﴾ [Al-Hajj: 65] And hear His true saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know.﴾ [Ghafir: 57]

So man changes and dies; but the heavens and the earth are stable until what Allah wills.

Yusuf, peace be upon him, says, continuing his supplication to Allah: ﴿You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter...﴾ [Yusuf: 101]

It is true that the Truthful One is Yusuf's Protector (wali) in this world; He has helped him, brought him near, and aided him, as evidenced by all the obstacles he passed through. Yusuf hopes and prays that Allah's bounty to him will not be limited to this perishing world, and that He will also reward him in the enduring, the Hereafter.

Since He, glorified is He, is his Protector in this world and the Hereafter, Yusuf calls upon Him: ﴿...Cause me to die in submission (Muslim) and join me with the righteous.﴾ [Yusuf: 101] His saying ﴿Cause me to die in submission...﴾ [Yusuf: 101] is only so that he may be worthy of Allah's bounty to him in the Hereafter; for Yusuf had taken the bounty of this world and enjoyed it, and provided for others with it, and walked in it in a way that pleases Allah.

When Yusuf wished for death, the scholars paused and said: "No one wished for it except Yusuf." For a person who is successful in this world is always found to be ambitious and eager for more good.

History records of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, that he accepted the governorship; whenever a soft garment was brought to him, he asked for one still softer, and when a tender food was brought to him, he asked for one still more tender.

When he became caliph, they would bring him a garment and he would ask for a rougher one; and those around him thought he was no longer consistent with himself, and they did not understand that he had a soul longing for what is better, always aspiring to the highest; when he yearned for the governorship it came to him, and when he yearned for the caliphate it came to him, and nothing remained after that except Paradise.

Maymun ibn Mihran, who was his companion, may Allah be pleased with both of them, once entered upon him and found him asking his Lord for death. He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, do you ask your Lord for death, when Allah has done through your hands much good; you have revived sunnahs and extinguished innovations; and your remaining is good for the Muslims?" Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said: "Shall I not be like the righteous servant when Allah completed His favour upon him and he said: ﴿...Cause me to die in submission and join me with the righteous.﴾ [Yusuf: 101]"

His saying ﴿Cause me to die in submission...﴾ [Yusuf: 101] consists of two parts: the first part: asking for death; the second part: that he die in submission. All of us are taken by death without asking for it; accordingly, the first part is not sought in itself, since it is inevitable, and what is sought is the second part, namely that Allah cause him to die in submission. That is why, when we come to graves, we say: "Peace be upon you, abode of a believing people; you have preceded us, and we, if Allah wills, will surely join you."

If someone asks: "Why do we say 'if Allah wills we will join you,' though we will certainly die?" We say: our saying "if Allah wills" is because of our desire to join them as believers.

Also, someone may ask: "Why does a prophet say to his Lord: ﴿...and join me with the righteous﴾ [Yusuf: 101]? Is there a righteous person who comes into this world without being guided by the methodology of a sent prophet?"

We say: the word "the righteous" (al-salihin) includes the prophets and others who believed in the message of heaven.

Thus the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him, ends; and the Truthful One then turns, after that conclusion, to the purpose of the story, which came complete in a single surah, unlike the rest of the Qur'an's narratives, which are scattered in separate glimpses in different places of the Noble Qur'an. The exception is the story of Nuh, which also came complete, to the extent that some superficial people said: "This is a repetition of the story in different glimpses." I always answer this by saying: it is a foundation of glimpses; if they are brought together, the story comes complete.

The Truthful One willed that the glimpses come scattered, because each glimpse came for a particular occasion, and all Qur'anic narrative came to strengthen the heart of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, because during his prophetic life, which lasted twenty-three years, he was exposed to grave events. Every moment needed strengthening, so the Truthful One sends down what He strengthens the heart of His Messenger with, clarifying at one place: do not grieve, for those messengers before you experienced such and such. Indeed, you may find in a single event two glimpses, as came concerning the enmity between Musa and Pharaoh. The Truthful One said: ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief...﴾ [Al-Qasas: 8] Here the enmity is from the side of Musa's adversaries. He says on the same matter as well: ﴿...let him take him, an enemy to Me and an enemy to him...﴾ [Ta-Ha: 39] Here the enmity is from two sides; because enmity becomes active when it comes from two sides, and enmity from one side alone cannot continue; and a battle arises from such enmity, but when enmity is from two sides, that prolongs the duration of the battle.

The second example is the saying of the Truthful One in the same story of Musa, a glimpse that occurred in the early days of Musa's life, before he was cast

The Almighty says at the end of the story: ﴿This is among the news of the unseen...﴾

"That" refers to this story, and the address is directed to Muhammad (ﷺ). That is: you, O Muhammad, were not with them when they said: ﴿Joseph and his brother are dearer to our father than we are...﴾ [Yusuf: 8]. So Allah, glory be to Him, informed you of news whose events you did not witness. The unseen (al-ghayb), as we have known before, is what is hidden from you but not hidden from others, and this is relative unseen (ghayb nisbi). There is also the absolute unseen (al-ghayb al-mutlaq), which is hidden from you and from people like you. As we know, the unseen has three barriers. The first is the barrier of past time that you did not witness, or the barrier of future time that has not yet come. The second is the barrier of place. The third is the barrier of the present, meaning that there are things happening in a place where you are not present, so you know nothing of their events. As for ﴿We reveal it to you...﴾ [Yusuf: 102], it means that We inform you of it by a hidden means, at the time when they gathered to agree on either killing Joseph or throwing him into the bottom of the well. Allah, glory be to Him, uncovered for you the barrier of the past regarding a matter He had not taught to the Messenger of Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) did not witness what passed between the brothers directly, nor did he hear it from a teacher, nor did he read about it, because he (ﷺ) was ummi (unlettered), one who had not learned reading or writing. He, glory be to Him, says about His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿You did not recite any scripture before it, nor did you write one with your right hand; otherwise the falsifiers would have had doubts﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 48]. They, by their own testimony, knew every movement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) before he was sent: his residence, his travels, and whom he met. Had they known that he had read a book, they would have had an argument, and even in the matter in which they had lost their insight, they said: ﴿It is only a human who teaches him﴾ [al-Nahl: 103]. Allah, glory be to Him, replied to them: ﴿...the tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Nahl: 103]. Allah, glory be to Him, refuted this argument. He has related to His Messenger much of the news of the unseen, and we have previously said much about this in "Ma Kunnat al-Qur'an" (What You Did Not Know of the Qur'an), such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿...You were not with them when they cast their pens to see which of them would take charge of Maryam, nor were you with them when they disputed﴾ [Al 'Imran: 44], and His saying, the Truth: ﴿You were not on the western side when We decreed the command to Musa, nor were you among the witnesses﴾ [al-Qasas: 44]. So it is as if the source of the Messenger's knowledge of all of that was Allah's informing him. The People of the Cave received what they asked to know of Joseph's story with obstinacy and denial, although they had made this request under the instigation of the Jews. He (ﷺ) brought them the story of Joseph in one place, at one time, and in one surah, not in scattered fragments as with most of the Qur'an's stories. He brought it to them complete, because they had not asked for a part of it, but had asked him about the story in its entirety, and they expected him to fail to do so. But he did not fail; rather, he brought them what they had asked for.

It should have occurred to them that Allah is the One who sent him, the One who taught him, and the One who informed him. But they did not believe, and this grieved the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah, glory be to Him, made clear to him: do not be distressed or despair: ﴿Perhaps you will destroy yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 3]. He, glory be to Him, also says to him: ﴿So perhaps you will destroy yourself with grief over their traces if they do not believe in this message﴾ [al-Kahf: 6]. You, O Messenger of Allah, are only obligated to convey. The Truth mentions this to console His Messenger (ﷺ) when he saw the obstinacy of the disbelievers, after he had brought them what they asked for and they then denied it: ﴿They denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance...﴾ [al-Naml: 14]. They denied what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought because they were keen only on worldly power, and it was necessary for them to believe in what he brought them. But stubbornness stood between them and the reality of certainty and the reality of faith. You cannot confront the stubborn person with proof or logic, for they want the weak to remain slaves, and to remain in control of creation through their tyranny, while the religion will make all people equal, and they hate that matter.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, moves on to a cosmic principle, saying: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you were eager, will not be believers.ﴩ

You, O Muhammad, will not make all people believers, even if you strive for that. The Prophet (ﷺ) was extremely keen that his people should believe, and he was one of them. Concerning him, the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; [he is] concerned over you and to the believers, kind and merciful.﴾ [at-Tawbah: 128] Yet they denied what had come to them with, and that matter saddened him. Regarding eagerness, we find a verse specifically concerning the Jews, those who prompted the people of Makkah to ask the Messenger (ﷺ) about the story of Yusuf. The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And you will surely find them the most eager of people for life...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 96] The people of Makkah were obligated to believe, since it had been established for them by clear proofs that he was a messenger from Allah. The saying of the Truth comes: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you were eager, will not be believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103]. This statement is a consolation from the Truth, glorified is He, to His Messenger, and to confirm for him that this is not only the condition of the people of Makkah, but this is the nature of most people. Why? Because most of them do not properly measure what the method of Allah gives them in this world and the Hereafter. When a person turns to the method of Allah, he measures his turning to this method by what it gives him in the Hereafter. He will then know that however much he gives himself of the pleasures of this world, his lifespan in it is appointed by the measure Allah has decreed for him, and life may end at any moment. When the Truth, glorified is He, concealed from people their lifespans in this world, this concealment was not vagueness, as some think; this vagueness is in reality the very essence of clarification, for the spread of the awareness that death can occur at any time puts a person in a state of watchfulness. Therefore, sudden deaths have a wisdom: that every person knows death has no cause, but rather is itself a cause in its own right; whether death occurs in an accident, through illness, or suddenly. A person enjoys this world according to his determined lifespan appointed by Allah, while in the Hereafter he enjoys according to the provisions of the Creator, glorified is He. The believing person measures his enjoyment in the Hereafter by Allah's power to give, and by the capacities of the Truth, not the capacities of creation. Suppose a person is cut off from the matter of the Hereafter, meaning he is a disbeliever in the Hereafter and takes it on the basis of this world alone; we say to him: look at what is demanded of you as prohibitions, and what is demanded of you as commands, and do not make it only for yourself, but make it for the millions of others opposite you. You will find that the prohibitions of the method, if they restrain you from an evil you would do to others, have also restrained others from doing evil to you; in this there is a benefit for you by material measures in which religion has no part. This matter must be taken within the framework of the principle that "preventing harm takes precedence over securing benefit" (dar' al-mafsadah muqaddam 'ala jalb al-maslahah). Suppose a person who loves you holds an apple and wants to throw it to you, while another person who hates you tries to throw a stone at you at the same moment, and both release what is in their hands toward you; here you must deflect the stone before catching the apple. Thus, preventing harm takes precedence over securing benefit.

A person must measure this in every matter, because many of the tools of civilizations, the innovations of modern society, or scientific inventions may give us some benefit, but it becomes clear that afterward they have much harm. An example of this is the invention of the substance "D.D.T." which killed some insects, and along with them killed many beneficial birds. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge...﴾ [al-Isra: 36] You must study any invention before using it, so that you see its benefit and harm before you use it. We have seen people who bring electricity into their homes trying to raise the electrical outlet ("fish") above the level children can reach, so that a child does not lose his fingers in those openings and get electrocuted; and we have found some engineers who designed devices that cut off electricity automatically if a human hand touches them. This is preventing harm taking precedence over securing benefit, and we must take precautions for such matters. In the verse about which we are reflecting, the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you were eager, will not be believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103]. Does His saying ﴿most of mankind...﴾ [Yusuf: 103] refer to those who do not believe, meaning that believers are a minority? We say: no; because "most" (akthar) may be contrasted with "fewer" (aqall), and it may be contrasted with "many" (kathir). The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Have you not considered that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures and many of mankind, and many deserve punishment...﴾ [al-Hajj: 18]. Thus we find that the word "many" may also be contrasted with the word "many." The Truth, glorified is He, made clear to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that even if he were eager, he could not make most people believers. Eagerness (hirs) is the attachment of the soul and the mobilization of effort to retain a thing that we see as bringing us benefit or removing harm, and it is a grasping that requires effort. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, clarifies to him: you will not guide whom you are eager to guide. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide one who misleads...﴾ [an-Nahl: 37]. From this verse we learn that every messenger must prepare himself for the fact that people will make comparisons between beneficial alternatives, and they will fall into errors of choosing what is not suitable for their long-term benefit; so prepare yourself for that, O Muhammad. And if you, O Messenger of Allah, have carried the message and ask them to believe for their own benefit, you do so without reward; although if they were to reflect on the matter, they should have appointed a reward for one who guides them to the right path, because reward is given to whoever provides you with a benefit.

A person is eager to pay a reward to whoever helps him gain a benefit; and the benefit is either limited to a worldly time that ends, or it is a benefit extending without end: comfort in this world and happiness in the Hereafter. The Qur'an brings the saying of the messengers: ﴿I do not ask you for it any reward...﴾ [al-An'am: 90], and two did not say this: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and Musa, peace be upon him. Reason would say: it should have been incumbent upon people, if they judged soundly, to pay a reward to the Messenger who explains to them the conditions of the cosmos, reassures them about their fate after death, explains to them the method of the Truth, and serves as a good example for them. In our contemporary world we find that families pay a great deal to a private tutor who teaches the son the principles of reading and writing; so what of one who illuminates sight and insight with guidance? The matter entails that the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, provides an everlasting benefit to whoever follows him, yet he did not ask for a reward.

Al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), on surah 12, verse 104:

The Exalted says: ﴿And you do not ask them for any wage for it...﴾

In this noble statement there is clarification that the Prophet (ﷺ) does not ask his people for a wage in return for guiding them, because his reward is with Allah alone. The Exalted also says: ﴿Or do you ask them for a wage, so that they are burdened by debt?﴾ [al-Tur: 40]. And the Exalted says, speaking on the tongue of His Messenger in another place: ﴿Say: "Whatever wage I have asked of you, it is yours. My wage is only with Allah..."﴾ [Saba: 47]. Here he elevates the wage: rather than taking it from one who is limited in his ability to pay, he seeks it from the One whose capacity to give reward is not limited. It is as if the work he does can be rewarded only by Allah, because the work he performs is according to the method of Allah and from Allah, so its reward can only come from none other than Allah. For this reason He says: ﴿...It is only a reminder to the worlds﴾ [Yusuf: 104].

The word "dhikr" (remembrance, reminder) has many usages, and the root dh-k-r is derived from "adh-dhakira" (memory). We have already learned that a human being has instruments of reception, which are the human senses, and information or experiences pass from them to the mental processes. That information passes through the focus of consciousness (bu'rat al-shu'ur), where it is kept for a period in this focus, then moves to the margin of consciousness (hashiyat al-shu'ur), until events call it up, and it returns once more to the focus of consciousness. For this reason, when you recall an old piece of information you say, "I have remembered it," as if the information were present somewhere in yourself but was not in the focus of consciousness. When the process of recall comes, it moves from the margin of consciousness to the focus of consciousness. Remembrance (al-tadhakkur) is: the summoning of information from the margin of consciousness to the focus of consciousness. The Exalted says: ﴿And remind them of the days of Allah...﴾ [Ibrahim: 5], meaning: remind them of what passed over them of events which Allah brought about, and which are not now present in the focus of their consciousness. The Qur'an is called "dhikr" because it reminds every believer in it of Allah, who has graciously given us the method by which our lives proceed toward the good of this world and the Hereafter. Thus remembrance is an aid to the intelligent person, and it is part of Allah's mercy toward creation: He did not leave creation preoccupied with the blessings so as to forget the One who bestowed them. This universe is organized with precise and wondrous exactness, and it contains everything that sustains human life. Among Allah's favors upon them is that He sent messengers as reminders of this divine bounty. The word "dhikr" indicates that the innate nature (fitrah) of the human being should have remained aware and mindful of Allah, but Allah decreed the heedlessness of events, so He placed the entire reminder in the noble Qur'an.

The Almighty says after that: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while turning away from it...﴾

When you hear "ka'ayyin" (how many), understand that it means "many, many, many," beyond counting. Like "ka'ayyin" is the word "kam" (how many). Counting is the sign of limiting, and that which exceeds limit is something one turns away from counting. No one can count the sands of the desert, for example. But each of us counts the money the seller returns to us after taking the price of what we bought. So turning away from counting means that the matter we want to count exceeds limit, and no one counts or enumerates the stars. This is why the Almighty draws our attention to this matter, to bestow His blessings upon His creation, and says: ﴿And if you tried to count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate it﴾ [Ibrahim: 34]. "In" here is for a matter that is doubted, and you will never be able to count the favour of Allah, because it exceeds limit. What is counted is always repeated. Here the Almighty mentioned one blessing without specifying it, because any blessing you receive from Allah, if you were to examine it thoroughly, you would find in it blessings that cannot be limited or counted.

So the word "ka'ayyin" means "kam." You say to a child who did not study his lessons: "How many times have I advised you?" You only say this after your patience has overflowed. "Kam" is also used to express magnifying the number, not from you the speaker, but from the one to whom the speech is addressed, as if you are entrusting him that he will only speak the truth, or as if you have recalled the advice and found it very numerous. A question about quantity is either asked by the speaker, or it is directed to the addressee. Asking the addressee is evidence that he will confess against himself, and confession is the master of proofs. When the Almighty says ﴿And how many...﴾ [Yusuf: 105], its meaning is that what follows it is abundant. Glorified is the One who said: ﴿And how many a prophet fought, and with him many devoted followers. They did not weaken for what afflicted them in the way of Allah, nor did they weaken or submit. And Allah loves the steadfast﴾ [Al 'Imran: 146]. Thus we understand that "ka'ayyin" means a very great quantity, one that has reached such abundance that it justifies our excuse before others if we fail to count it.

"Ayat" is the plural of "ayah" (sign, verse), which is a wondrous thing that draws attention. It is said: "So-and-so is an ayah in intelligence," meaning his intelligence is proverbial, a wondrous matter that surpasses the intelligence of others. It is said: "So-and-so is an ayah in courage," and so on. The meaning of a wondrous thing is that it departs from the familiar and is not forgotten. The Almighty has scattered wondrous signs throughout the universe, and everything scattered in the universe has a wisdom. The meanings of the ayat are divided into three. The first: the cosmic signs we have spoken of, which are wonders. They are a proof for the contemplator to believe in Allah who brought them into being. They turn you to the fact that the One who created them must possess perfect wisdom and perfect precision, and these signs draw our attention to the truth of the Oneness of Allah and belief in Him. The Almighty has scattered these signs in the universe.

When Allah, through His messengers, announced that He is the One who created them, and no one else has claimed "I am the one who created," this matter of creation is established for Him, glorified be He. He is the Creator, and all else is created. These signs were created for a purpose and an end. In Surat al-Rum we find verses that gather most of the signs of the universe, where the Almighty says: ﴿So glorified is Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning. And to Him is praise in the heavens and the earth, and at night and when you are at noon. He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living and gives life to the earth after its death. And thus you will be brought out. And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then suddenly you are human beings dispersing. And among His signs is that He created for you from yourselves spouses that you may find tranquillity in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought. And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages and your colours. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge. And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen. And among His signs He shows you lightning, producing fear and hope, and sends down from the sky water by which He gives life to the earth after its death. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason. And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command. Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you will come out﴾ [Al-Rum: 17-25]. All these are signs that alert the human being within the universe that he enjoys it according to supreme laws, in which lies the secret of the continuation of his life, so he must pay attention to the One who brought them into being. After he becomes aware of a Supreme Existence, he must ask: what does this Supreme Creator want from him? These signs logically compel us that there must exist one who conveys to us what the Supreme Possessor requires. When a messenger comes and tells us: the One you seek is named Allah, and He has sent me to convey to you what He requires of you, that you worship Him, follow His commands and avoid His prohibitions.

The second type of signs are miraculous signs, and their purpose is to confirm the call of the messengers. It was necessary that each messenger come with a sign to establish the truthfulness of his message from Allah, because every messenger is a human being, and he must have a sign that breaks the laws, and these are the miracles that came with the messengers. There are also legal signs, which are the third type, and these are the verses (divisions) that carry sentences containing the rulings of the Noble Qur'an, the final method. These too are wondrous signs, because you will not find a ruling of the religion that does not logically touch a need of the human soul. Even if people disbelieve, they will be compelled to many matters they used to deny, yet there is no solution to the problems they face except through them. A clear example is divorce. They criticised Islam for bringing it, saying that such a solution for the relationship between man and woman may carry much harshness on the family. But they resorted to it after the events of life had bitten them, and thus the human mind was guided to a ruling that it had once contradicted.

Likewise the matter of usury (riba), for which they are now trying to devise a system to free themselves from usury entirely, saying: nothing prevents the human mind from reaching what is beneficial. Thus we find that the cosmic signs are wonders by every measure, the signs accompanying the messengers are miracles that broke the laws, and the signs of the Qur'an, with the rulings it contains, protect the human being from disease before it occurs, and the difficulties of life compel them to return to the rulings of the Qur'an to adopt them. Yet they turn away from all the signs: they turn away from the signs of the universe which, if they examined them carefully, would establish for them the existence of a Creator God, and they would receive a gift from the gifts of Allah that would spread education and development. All modern discoveries have come only as a result of observations of some phenomenon in the universe. I have already given the example of the man who sat to cook in a pot, then saw the lid of the pot rising, and he thought and asked: why does the lid of the pot rise? The man did not turn away from reflecting on this, and deducing the truth of water turning into vapour, and through that he was able to discover that water, when it evaporates, expands and needs a space larger than the space it occupied before expansion. This reflection was behind the discovery of steam power, by which ships and trains operated, and an age called "the age of steam" began. And this one who saw a vessel float on the surface of water and reflected on that phenomenon, and formulated a principle bearing his name, which is "Archimedes' principle." Thus we find that anyone who contemplates the universe precisely will find in its phenomena what benefits the world, just as the world benefited from the reflections of Archimedes and others, who presented their reflections as observations, which scientists followed to reach inventions that benefit humanity. Thus we see that the Almighty does not withhold from the disbeliever what benefits the world, as long as he contemplates the phenomena of the universe and deduces from them what benefits humanity.

So the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while turning away from it...﴾ [Yusuf: 105]: if you want it as a means to faith in a God, it leads you to faith; and if you want it for the benefit of this world, then the Truth has not withheld from a disbeliever giving him the result of the effort he exerts. The whole requirement is that you do not pass by the signs of Allah while turning away from them, but that a person approach them with the attentiveness of a student, either to arrive at a matter of faith that enriches your life and gives you a life without end, which is the life of the Hereafter, or to make your life and the lives of others happy, by innovating things that benefit you and benefit humanity.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they associate others with Him.﴾

Thus we see the filters that people pass through to reach faith. The first filter is His saying: ﴿And most of mankind will not believe, however eager you are.﴾ [Yusuf: 103] That is, most people will not reach faith, even if the Messenger (ﷺ) was eager for them to believe. We have said that the opposite of "many" (kathir) may be "few" (qalil), and it may also be "many." Some believers may have their faith mixed with a trace of shirk. It is true that they believe in the One God, but their faith is not certain. It is a wavering faith, and they associate others with Him.

The second filter is His saying: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they associate others with Him.﴾ [Yusuf: 106] An example of this is the disbelievers of Quraysh, about whom the Exalted says: ﴿If you asked them who created them, they would surely say, "God..."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87] He also says about them: ﴿If you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "God..."﴾ [Luqman: 25] Despite this statement, they took intercessors for themselves with God, and they said that the angels are daughters of God. Thus they set up partners with God. Along with them is everyone among the People of the Book who claimed that God has a son. Also, along with these there are some Muslims who single out powerful people for a submission that cannot be called affection by custom, because it is a drawing near filled with humiliation. They believe that these people have influence over benefit and harm, and this is a kind of shirk. One of them comes to a person of influence and says: "I hope you will fulfill this matter for me." The person of influence replies: "Rely on God, and God willing, God will fulfill your need." But the one seeking the favor goes further in humiliation and says: "I also rely on you, that you fulfill this need for me." Or the person of influence replies and says: "I will do such-and-such for you, and the rest is up to God." When I hear this, I ask myself: what about the one who is not remaining, is he not also up to God?

God scatters wisdom in things that their owners wished for. Those things were granted, and then it became clear that there was evil in them. And there are things their owners wished for that were not granted, and then it became clear that not granting them contained all the good. We find the saying: "Seek things with the dignity of your souls, for affairs proceed by divine decrees."

Perhaps a refusal displeases you, yet the refusal was better for you than granting it to you, for the refusal is the very essence of giving. Therefore a person should always know that God is the Doer and the Causer, and that the means are something else. I always remind that when we perform Hajj or 'Umrah, we walk between al-Safa and al-Marwa to remember what our lady Hajar did when she walked between al-Safa and al-Marwa, seeking water for her infant after she had exhausted her means. Then she found water beneath the foot of her infant Isma'il. She took up the means, so the Lord of the means brought her what she asked for. The Exalted did not bring her water at al-Safa or al-Marwa, in order to confirm for her the first matter about which she had asked Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when he settled her in this place.

She said to him: "Did you settle us here by your own opinion, or did God command you to do this?" He said: "Yes, my Lord commanded me." She said: "Then He will not waste us." She walked searching for water, taking up the means, and she found water by the power of the Supreme Causer.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And most of them do not believe in God except that they associate others with Him.﴾ [Yusuf: 106] requires us to know how shirk seeps into faith. We may ask: since faith exists, from where does the moment of shirk come? The Exalted explains this to us when He says: ﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him. * So that they may deny what We have given them and enjoy themselves. But they will soon know.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 65-66] Thus they had believed while they were in the ship, and they began to call upon God when a crisis overtook them at sea. But as soon as they reached the shore, shirk appeared among them. If someone asks them: "What happened?" they answer that they had taken their precautions and prepared lifeboats. They forgot that it was God who saved them, and so the saying of the Exalted applied to them: ﴿And they set up rivals to God to mislead from His way. Say: "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾ [Ibrahim: 30]

In our daily lives, you may go to meet someone's need, and after God makes it easy for you to fulfill that need, you turn around and do not find him, and he does not think to thank you. When you meet him, he says: "Everything you asked of me has been fulfilled. I spoke to so-and-so and he fulfilled it." He says this in order to remove from you the favor God bestowed upon you by your fulfilling his need. That is because at the moment he asked you for help with that need, he was humbled and submissive, but once it was fulfilled he acts like Pharaoh and forgets. Only seeing you will pull him out of his arrogance, because he knows that you have a favor upon him. He may even intend evil toward you, despite the fact that you are the one who did good to him. Why? Because this is the nature of man. The Exalted says: ﴿No! Indeed, man transgresses * whenever he sees himself self-sufficient.﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6-7] Therefore the proverb says: "Beware the evil of the one to whom you have done good." You guard against his evil by taking care not to remind him of your kindness, so that you do not cultivate in him the instinct of hatred toward you.

The sincere person reckons any help he gives to others as something to be credited with God. He takes his reward from his Creator at the moment of doing the good deed, and expects nothing from the one to whom he did good. This is because you do not know what he thought at the moment you did him the service. When he sees people welcoming you in the place where you serve him, he may wonder: "Why do they respect you more than him?" He asks this question of himself, even though you are present with him in this place to serve him. For this reason, common people say this proverb: "Do good and throw it into the sea," because it is God who rewards you, not people. So make all your deeds directed to God, and forget that you have done a kindness to anyone.

The concealed kindness is the most beneficial kind of kindness for you, because the One who rewards it is God, and He, glory be to Him, will hand you its reward and its recompense with His own hand. Therefore you must forget the one to whom you have done good, so that God may compensate you with good for what you did. It is said in a narration that Musa (peace be upon him) said: "O my Lord, I ask You that nothing be said about me that is not in me." God made it clear to him: "O Musa, I did not make it for Myself, so how would I make it for you?" The Exalted presents this matter in the Qur'an in another form, saying: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He bestows on him a favor from Himself, he forgets what he had been calling upon Him for before, and he sets up rivals to God to mislead from His way. Say: "Enjoy your disbelief briefly; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire."﴾ [al-Zumar: 8]

When harm touches a person, he calls upon the Lordship (rububiyyah), the One who takes charge of his interests: "O my Lord, You are the One who created me, and You are the One who takes charge of my upbringing. I rely on You for my interests, so rescue me from what I am in." Such a person is like the captain whom God saves by a miracle from the storm, but after the rescue he tries to attribute the ship's escape from drowning to himself. Therefore I always say: beware, O believers, lest you forget the Bestower, the Causer in everything. Beware of being seduced by the means, so that you become heedless of the Causer, who is the Giver of the means. I say this so that you do not fall into wronging yourselves by associating others with God. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with injustice, for them is security, and they are guided.﴾ [al-An'am: 82] Injustice, as we know, is giving something that belongs to another to someone other than its owner. So how would anyone dare to ignore God's favor upon him, and fall into hidden shirk? The greatest injustice is shirk. The Exalted says: ﴿... Indeed, association (with Him) is great injustice.﴾ [Luqman: 13]

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Do they feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming calamity...﴾

Have these people not reckoned with God's retribution against them in the form of the punishment of this world, which is all-encompassing? For the overwhelming calamity (al-ghashiyah) is the punishment that encompasses and covers everyone. Or is it that they consider the death and the Resurrection with its punishment to be far off, even though death is hung around the necks of all, and no one knows the time of his death? The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies, his resurrection has come." So what is it that delays them from believing in God and devoting themselves to His Oneness, without shirk touching them, before their Resurrection comes upon them suddenly; that is, without any preliminary warning?

We know that those who have preceded us to death do not perceive the passage of time for long until the Resurrection of all creation arrives, because time only seems long to one who follows its events. The sleeper, for example, does not know how long he has slept, because his consciousness is absent and so he does not know time. What makes it clear to us that those who have gone before us do not feel the passage of time is the saying of the Truth: ﴿As if they had tarried but an evening or a morning of it, on the day they see it﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 12, verse 108:

The saying of the Truth, glorified is He, follows after that: ﴿Say: This is my way; I call to Allah upon insight, I and whoever follows me. And glory be to Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Him.﴾

That is: Say, O Muhammad, "This is my method." The sabil (way, path), as we know, is the road. The saying of the Truth, ﴿This is my way﴾ [Yusuf: 108], shows that the word sabil comes sometimes feminine, as in this verse, and sometimes masculine, as in the saying of the Truth: ﴿And if they see the way of right guidance, they will not take it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will take it as a way﴾ [al-A'raf: 146]. And proclaim, O Muhammad, that this call which you have brought is for belief in the One God. He, glorified is He, does not benefit from the method that was revealed to you so that the servants may apply it; rather, in it is the good of their lives. He, glorified is He, is Allah: He is the First before everything, without beginning, and the Remaining after every existent, without end. Along with the creation of the creatures, those who believe, He is Allah; and if they all disbelieve, He is Allah. The matter of the legal responsibility for the method returns to you yourselves: whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve. Let us read the saying of the Truth: ﴿When the heaven is split asunder, and has listened to its Lord and it is right that it should⟩ [al-Inshiqaq: 1-2]. It splits immediately upon hearing the command of Allah, and the moment of reckoning comes.

The saying of the Truth, ﴿Say: This is my way; I call to Allah upon insight⟩ [Yusuf: 108], means: I call by the path that leads to Allah, in belief in Him and acceptance of His method, and seeking what He has of reward in the Hereafter; and I am upon insight regarding what I call to. Sight, as we know, is for the sensible things, and insight (basirah) is for the non-sensible things. Physical sight does not perform the very work of insight, because insight is a certainty accompanied by a light that convinces the human soul, even if the apparent matters do not compel conviction. An example of this: the mother of Musa, when Allah inspired her to cast her son into the river (al-yamm). Had she measured this matter by her intellect, she would not have accepted it; but by insight she accepted it, because it came from Allah, with no opponent from the human soul. So insight is certainty and light founded on proof from the heart; the servant obeys it with obedience by entrusting, and it is said: faith is obedience with insight.

We may read the saying of the Truth: ﴿Say: This is my way; I call to Allah upon insight⟩ [Yusuf: 108] as a complete sentence, and then read after it: ﴿I and whoever follows me⟩ [Yusuf: 108], or read it in full: ﴿Say: This is my way; I call to Allah upon insight, I and whoever follows me. And glory be to Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Him⟩ [Yusuf: 108]. The saying of the Truth, ﴿And glory be to Allah⟩ [Yusuf: 108], means: He, glorified is He, is absolutely transcendent in His essence, so no essence resembles Him; His essence is not confined to the material form like yours, into which the soul is breathed. He, glorified is He, is absolutely transcendent in His acts, so no act resembles His act. Likewise His attributes are not like the attributes of humans. When you know that Allah hears and sees, take that within the scope of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him⟩ [al-Shura: 11]. Likewise His existence, glorified is He, is not like your existence, because His existence is the existence of the self-subsisting, eternal Possessor, while you are a newly arisen occurrence in the universe that He created, glorified is He. For this reason some people measured the journey of the Night Ascent (al-Isra' wa al-Mi'raj) by the power of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and did not notice that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I was taken by night." And the saying of the Truth, glorified is He, was revealed: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, that We might show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing⟩ [al-Isra': 1]. Thus you know that the deed was not by the power of Muhammad ﷺ, but by the power of the One who created the whole universe, capable of everything, whom no true believer can associate with Him, in the face of this proof.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 12, verse 109:

The Truthful Lord (al-Haqq) says after that: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns...﴾

Here the Lord, glory be to Him, turns to the messengers who came before Muhammad (ﷺ). The Lord says: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra: 94] That is, they were seeking a messenger from other than humankind, and this matter had not occurred before. Had it occurred before, they would have said, "And why did He do it with others than us?" Therefore He, glory be to Him, wanted to return their reason to them, so He said: ﴿Say, "If there were in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."﴾ [al-Isra: 95] Angels, by their nature, cannot live on the earth, and they are not fit to be a model or a behavioural example (uswa) for humans. The Lord says of the angels: ﴿...they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded.﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6] An angel cannot be a model for a human being, because the angel is an unseen creation, not perceptible to humans; and if God had willed him to be a messenger, He would have embodied him as a human. And if He had made him a human, the doubt would have remained as it is. Or: the verse came to close the avenues that were opened to people afterwards in the wars of apostasy (ridda), when Sajah claimed that she was a prophetess sent (by God).

Therefore the Lord, from the beginning, said: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed...﴾ [Yusuf: 109] to clarify for us that a woman cannot be a messenger from Him, glory be to Him; because the task of the messenger is to join the world in the manner of conveying a message, and a woman is required to be a dwelling (sakan). Also, the messenger is presumed not to be relieved of any devotional obligation (taklif ta'abbudi) at any time, whereas a woman is relieved of the devotional obligation during menstruation (al-tamth), and the task of the messenger requires that he be fully fulfilling the obligatory duties at all times. Then how could they ask for that, when among the tasks of the messengers before was only men, and the Truth did not ask any of them, and did not seek permission from any of the earlier messengers to take up his mission; rather he received the charge from God without choosing it, and receives what he is commanded to convey to the people, and the command comes through revelation. And revelation, as we know, is informing in secrecy, and it is applied absolutely only to conveying from God. And there was no messenger delegated to convey what he loves or to legislate; rather every messenger was charged with conveying what he is sent with, except Muhammad (ﷺ), for the Truthful Lord delegated to him the authority to legislate, and it was revealed in the Qur'an: ﴿Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it...﴾ [al-Hashr: 7] The Lord says of these earlier messengers that they were: ﴿from the people of the towns...﴾ [Yusuf: 109] The town (qarya) held the same status in our contemporary world as the city (madina). When you visit the people of the city, you find goodness among them, unlike the people of the desert (badiya): the Bedouin among them may not find anything to offer you, as the udder of the livestock may have dried up, or he may not find a sheep to slaughter for you.

﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns. Have they not travelled in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? And the abode of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Will you not then reason?﴾

The difference between the people of the town and the people of the desert is that the people of the town have settlement (tawattun); they possess the capacity to coexist with others, their interests are linked to one another, their feelings toward each other are tender, their perceptions are broadened by diverse knowledge, and they lack the harshness of the people of the desert. The Bedouin among them owns nothing but the saddle on the back of his camel; he seeks water sources and pastures for the livestock he grazes. Thus among the people of the towns there is tenderness, knowledge, and courtesy in dealing and in conduct; therefore no messenger came from the Bedouins, so that his knowledge would not be deficient and he would not be coarse, possessing harshness of speech and conduct. The messenger is presumed to receive everyone he meets with gentleness, kindness, and good companionship; therefore he is generally from the people of the towns, because they are not cruel and are not ignorant of the affairs of social coexistence. The Lord continues: ﴿Have they not travelled in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them...﴾ [Yusuf: 109] That is, if they do not believe in an Hereafter to which they return, and do not know when they will return, then let them take this world as a measure; let them look across the expanse of the earth and see what happened to those who denied the messengers. They will find that destruction and punishment have befallen every denier. Had they travelled in the earth and looked with the eye of reflection, they would have seen the towns of those who hewed their houses in the mountains, which the Lord laid waste, and they would have seen that the Lord poured the whip of punishment upon the people of 'Ad and the household of Pharaoh. So if you do not fear the Hereafter, then you must fear the punishment of this world. The Lord's saying: ﴿Have they not travelled in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them...﴾ [Yusuf: 109] is one of the cosmic allusions (lafatat al-kawniyat) in the Qur'an. In former times we did not know that there is an atmospheric envelope surrounding the earth, and we did not know that this atmospheric envelope contains the oxygen we need for breathing. We did not know that this atmospheric envelope is part of the completeness of the earth, and that when you walk on dry land, the atmospheric envelope is above you; thus you are walking on the earth, because what is above you of atmosphere is an appendage of the earth. Travelling in the earth is for sightseeing in it, and sightseeing in the earth is of two kinds: sightseeing of reflection (i'tibar), and sightseeing of exploitation (istithmar). The Lord expresses sightseeing of reflection by saying: ﴿Have they not travelled in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them...﴾ [al-Rum: 9] and He expresses sightseeing of exploitation by saying: ﴿Say, "Travel in the earth and observe how He began creation; then Allah will produce the final creation..."﴾ [al-Ankabut: 20] So sightseeing of reflection is what draws you to the power of Allah, and sightseeing of exploitation is of cultivating the earth. The Lord says: ﴿And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find on the earth many a refuge and abundance...﴾ [al-Nisa: 100] You are charged with this task, and if a place on earth becomes narrow for you, then seek another place, according to the Lord's saying: ﴿Was not the earth of Allah spacious that you could emigrate therein...﴾ [al-Nisa: 97] You may exploit as you wish, on condition that exploitation does not distract you from reflection. The Lord continues: ﴿how was the end of those before them...﴾ [Yusuf: 109] Would that the matter were limited to the retribution that befell them in this world; rather there is a more severe retribution awaiting them in the Hereafter. The Lord says: ﴿...and the abode of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Will you not then reason?﴾ [Yusuf: 109] The Lord's discourse about the fate of those who denied appears to us as the counterpart to what awaits the believers, and the verse did not mention the fate of these deniers by direct expression; this is called in the language ihtibak (a rhetorical device of implicit contrast). Like the Lord's saying: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?...﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41] Every day the land of disbelief diminishes and the expanse of faith grows. Thus punishment comes from Allah's side, and we take its counterpart in this world; and at another time He brings lasting reward for the believers, and we take its counterpart in the Hereafter. One might say: why did the Lord not say that He would bring them something worse than the punishment of this world on the Last Day? I say: it is the superficial rational context, which is not from Allah, that could remind them that the punishment of the Hereafter is worse than the punishment of this world. But the Lord does not say that; rather He turned from this to the counterpart regarding the believers, saying: ﴿...and the abode of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Will you not then reason?﴾ [Yusuf: 109] So when He brings punishment in this world for the disbelievers and then brings reward in the Hereafter for the God-fearing, one derives from this counterpart that those who are not believers will have a severe reckoning; and what indicates it there has been omitted here, so that we know how the Qur'anic composition is woven.

Then He, glorified is He, says after that: ﴿Until, when the messengers despaired...﴾

The word ﴿until﴾ [Yusuf: 110] indicates that there is an end-point, and since there is an end-point, there must have been a beginning that preceded it. We say: "I ate the fish until its head" (ḥattā ra'suhā). That is, the beginning was eating the fish, and the end was its head. The beginning that precedes ﴿the messengers despaired...﴾ [Yusuf: 110] is His word, the Truth: ﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed...﴾ [Yusuf: 109]. Since Allah, the Truth, has sent them, they had been guaranteed victory; but victory was delayed, so the messengers despaired. This delay was intended by Allah, the Truth, because He wants to entrust the believers with the task of guiding the movement of life on earth until the Hour is established, and so it must not be undertaken except by one who has been tested with precise testing. The exemplary messenger and those with him and those who follow them must pass through many trials, and whoever is patient through the trials and emerges successful is fit to bear the task. And He, the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise without there having come to you the example of those who passed away before you? Hardship and adversity touched them, and they were shaken, until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?"...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214]. So there must be a testing that purifies. In our own life's movement, we qualify the student academically so that he advances to the certificate of completing primary studies, then we qualify him to obtain the certificate of completing preparatory studies, then to obtain the certificate of completing secondary studies, then he joins the university and is tested annually until he graduates from university. If he wishes to complete his studies to obtain a master's and a doctorate, he exerts more effort. All that journey is so that he may take up the responsibility of the work assigned to him, for which he is worthy. How much more so, then, is the process of sending a messenger to a people? There must therefore be a purification of him and of those who follow him, so that only those who are utterly certain remain faithful to the covenant, certain that what they miss of the good of this world they will find better with Allah in the Hereafter.

Someone may say: Is it reasonable that the messengers should despair? We say: let us first understand the meaning of "istay'asa" (despaired); there is a difference between "ya's" and "istay'asa." "Ya's" means cutting off hope in something, while "istay'asa" means that one insists on cutting off hope; that is, hope has not yet been cut off. Whoever cuts off hope is one who has no outlet to hope, and a person's hope is only cut off if he believes in causes detached from their highest Causer. But if Allah has given him the causes, and then the causes come to an end without bringing him to a result, the believer in Allah is the one who says: "I am not concerned with causes, because with me is the Causer." Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿...And do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of the mercy of Allah except the disbelieving people.﴾ [Yusuf: 87]. Therefore we find that the highest rate of suicide is found among the disbelieving atheists, because they do not possess a store of faith that makes them believe that they have a Lord above all causes, capable of breaking the laws. As for the believer, he takes refuge in a firm pillar: the power of the Truth, glorified is He, the Causer of all causes, who is able to break the causes.

Why do the messengers despair? Because their eagerness for hastening victory prompted some of them to ask, as the believers asked: ﴿When is the help of Allah?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214], in addition to their thinking that they had been denied. The Truth, glorified is He, says here: ﴿and they thought that they had been denied...﴾ [Yusuf: 110]. The root letters "kaf," "dhal," and "ba'" give "kadhaba" (he lied), "kudhiba 'alayhi" (a lie was told about him), and "kudhdhiba" (he was denied). Lying is speech that contradicts reality, and the intelligent person is one who passes his words through his mind before he utters them. As for one who lacks sound judgment and is not capable of reflection, he speaks without thinking and does not pass his speech through his mind; therefore he is called "makhrif" (one who talks nonsense). We have already explained truthfulness, and said: it is the conformity of the verbal proposition with reality, while lying is the non-conformity of the verbal proposition with reality. Whoever says something he knows does not conform to reality is said to be deliberately lying; whoever says something that he judges most probably does not conform to reality, and transmits it from another, is lying without his lie being counted as fabrication. The person who is careful with precision conveys speech attributed to the one who said it to him, so he says, "So-and-so told me," and is not counted a liar. Therefore I always say: scholars must distinguish between the lying of the one who issues a fatwa, the lying of the report, and the lying of the reporter. The false report is the responsibility of whoever deliberately lied; but the transmitter of a report, as long as he has attributed it to the one who said it, his position is different.

In the verse about which we are reflecting, there are two readings: one reading is "wa-ẓannū annahum qad kudhibū" (and they thought that they had been lied to), meaning others related to them falsehood; and a second reading is "wa-ẓannū annahum qad kudhdhibū" (and they thought that they had been denied), meaning that they thought what had been said to them about victory was a lie. Someone may ask: how could the messengers think that? I say: when a messenger asks his people to believe, he knows that what confirms the truth of his message is the coming of victory; and some thoughts pass over him, fearing that the fighters with him would say, "He has lied to us," because ẓann (supposition) is a report of what is most probable. It does not occur to the messengers that Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, God forbid, has lied to them in His promise; rather they thought that victory would come to them quickly, and they took the slowness of victory's arrival as proof that victory would not come; or they feared that others would deny them. Therefore we find the Truth, glorified is He, informing His messengers that victory will come at the time He determines, which no one knows, for He does not hasten with the haste of His servants until matters reach what He wills. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And they thought that they had been denied; Our help came to them...﴾ [Yusuf: 110]. Thus victory comes after severe tremor, and its effect is like the effect of water on one who is parched with thirst; we can imagine the longing of the thirsty for a cup of water. Also, the delay of victory gives the disbelievers a delusion that makes them persist in their delusion; and when victory comes, the joy of the believers in the Messenger is multiplied, and likewise the grief of the disbelievers toward him is multiplied. The arrival of victory for the believers entails the defeat of the disbelievers, because that is the will of Allah, whose might and punishment fall upon those who disbelieve in Him.

Says the Exalted after that: ﴿Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding...﴾

We note that this verse came in Surah Yusuf; that is, if you want the story of Yusuf and his brothers, the surah contains the whole story with its aims, its objectives and its admonition. Or the point is in all the stories of the prophets. The Truth, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We relate to you from the news of the messengers that which We strengthen your heart thereby...﴾ [Hud: 120]. We know that the meaning of qasas (narrative, story) is taken from qassu al-athar (tracing the track), and following it without addition or reduction. The Truth, the Exalted, says here: ﴿Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding...﴾ [Yusuf: 111]. And at the beginning of the surah the Truth said: ﴿... if you are able to interpret dreams﴾ [Yusuf: 43]. We know that the root "ʿ-b-r" (ʿabara) indicates transfer from the apparent to the hidden. The lesson (ʿibrah) in this story, the story of Yusuf, and likewise all the stories of the Qur'an, we take from their apparent part a lesson applied to the hidden thing we face; so we do not do bad deeds, and we advance to good deeds. When we devote ourselves to the good deed that came in any Qur'anic story, and when we keep away from the bad deed whose report came in the Qur'anic story, thereby we have understood those stories well. For example: we find the wrongdoer in the Qur'anic stories, and in the story of Yusuf specifically, and he is overturned, so one of us takes the lesson and builds his life on not wronging anyone. And when a person among us sees the wronged one being victorious, he does not grieve if he is subjected to injustice, because he has taken the lesson from what awaits him of victory by God's permission. And we say: "ʿabara al-nahr" meaning he crossed from one bank to the other. Likewise our saying "taʿbur al-ruʾyā" meaning you interpret it, because dreams come symbolically, and you interpret them, that is, you explain them and transfer them from the hidden to the apparent, and clarify what is intended from them. We describe the tear as "ʿibrah," and the grief buried in the human soul is indicated by the tear. Here the Truth, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding...﴾ [Yusuf: 111]. The lesson may pass by, but only the intelligent one who scrutinizes things pays attention to it; as for the one who passes over it in haste, he gains nothing from it. "Ulu al-albab" are the people of sound minds, and "al-albab" is the plural of "lubb." The lubb is the essence of the desired thing; the husk exists to protect the kernel, and the intellect was called "lubb" because it casts the husks far away and gives us the essence of things and their good. The Truth, the Exalted, continues: ﴿It was not a narration invented, but a confirmation of what was before it...﴾ [Yusuf: 111]. That is: what came upon your tongue, O Muhammad, and what the Truth revealed to you as inspiration, is not a narrative of deliberate falsehood; rather it is the truth that agrees with the books that preceded it. It is said "bayna yadayk" meaning what preceded you; so if you are walking in a line, whoever is in front of you is called "bayna yadayk," and whoever is behind you is called "man khalfak."

The Qur'an came to confirm the books that preceded it, and it is not they that confirm it, because it is the dominant (muhaymin) Book, and the Truth, the Exalted, is the One who says: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book in truth, confirming what is before it of the Book and as a guardian over it...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48]. The Truth, the Exalted, adds in the same verse about which we are reflecting: ﴿and the detailed explanation of all things...﴾ [Yusuf: 111]. So the Qur'an confirms the previous books and details everything; that is, it gives each particular matter its ruling in a particular matter suitable to it. It is therefore not a general, vague speech; rather, the detailing of each ruling proceeds in accordance with every matter of human affairs. In our daily customs we say: "So-and-so bought a tailored suit (badlah tafsil)." That is, its measurements are perfectly suited to him and fitted to him when he wears it. In matters of belief we find, God forbid, one who says there is no god at all, and opposite him one who says the gods are many, because all the beings existing in the universe are hard for one god to create; so there is a god for the sky, a god for the earth, a god for plants, and a god for animals. We say to them: how can there be a god who is able to do one thing and unable to do another? And if these say, "those gods cooperate with one another," we reply: that is not divinity at all. Therefore we find the Truth, the Exalted, says: ﴿God presents an example: a man in whom are partners disputing, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise be to God, but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Zumar: 29]. When the partners are at odds, the condition of this slave owned by them lives in hardship and torment; but the man owned by one man has a different condition, because he acts on one command, so he lives at ease. We find the Truth, the Exalted, saying of the multiple gods: ﴿God has not taken any son, and there was not with Him any god; otherwise each god would have gone off with what he created, and some of them would have overcome others. Glory be to God above what they describe﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 91]. As for one who says there is no god in the universe, we say to him: is it conceivable that this whole precise, perfectly ordered universe exists without a maker? Therefore the Truth, the Exalted, willed to detail this matter to affirm that there is no god in the universe other than one God. We find the Qur'an details the rulings for us and sends down for each issue a ruling suited to it; so no ruling passes from one domain to another. Likewise the detailing of the verses: there is the muhkam and the mutashabih; and the parable is the saying of the Truth, the Exalted. ﴿And they hasten to the good things...﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 114], and He says in another place: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord...﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 133]. He came once with the word "ilā" and once with "fī," because each has its fitting and detailed placement according to its position. Hastening to forgiveness means that the one who hastens to it is outside it, and it is the goal he will reach; but the one who hastens in good things lives in goodness now, and we ask him to increase in good.

And also His saying: ﴿... and be patient over what befalls you; indeed that is of the resolute matters﴾ [Luqman: 17], and His saying: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the resolute matters﴾ [al-Shura: 43]. One of them came concerning calamities that have an opponent, and the other concerning calamities that have no opponent, such as illness, where there is no opponent and no enmity. But if someone strikes me, or attacks one of my children, he is my opponent and there is enmity; his presence before me stirs evil in my soul, and I need to restrain myself with firm resolve. This is the detailing of the Book. The Truth, the Exalted, says: ﴿A Book whose verses are detailed...﴾ [Fussilat: 3]; that is, every part of it is suited to the matter for which it was revealed. An example of this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty; We provide for them and for you...﴾ [al-Isra': 31], and the Truth's saying: ﴿And do not kill your children because of poverty; We provide for you and for them...﴾ [al-An'am: 151]. Each verse suits its place, its meaning is consistent within itself, and its detailing was completed in accordance with what it came for. So His saying: ﴿do not kill your children out of poverty...﴾ [al-An'am: 151] means that poverty exists and the person is preoccupied with his own provision over his son's provision. As for His saying: ﴿for fear of poverty...﴾ [al-Isra': 31], that means poverty is not yet present, and there is a fear that it will come upon the person; it is a fear of a matter that has not yet occurred. Thus we find in the Qur'an a detailing of everything you need in the affairs of your worldly life and your hereafter, and it is a detailing of everything you do not have. The hoopoe said of the Queen of Sheba, Bilqis: ﴿and she has been given of everything...﴾ [al-Naml: 23]. This does not mean she was given everything in this world; rather she was given everything she possesses, or could possess, in this world. The saying of the Truth, the Exalted: ﴿and the detailing of all things...﴾ [Yusuf: 111] does not mean that we ask, for example: "How many loaves are in a measure of wheat?" It once happened that someone asked Imam Muhammad 'Abduh this question; so he brought a baker and asked him this question, and the baker answered. The questioner said: "But you did not bring the answer from the Qur'an?" Imam Muhammad 'Abduh said: "Why do you not cite His saying, the Truth: ﴿... so ask the people of the reminder if you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 43]?" Thus we know that He, the Exalted, has not neglected anything in the Book. The Truth, the Exalted, concludes the noble verse with His saying: ﴿... and the detailing of all things, and a guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [Yusuf: 111]. We know that guidance (hudā) is the path leading to good, and this path leading to good divides into two parts: the first part is prevention from evil for one who has not fallen into it; the second part is treatment for one who has fallen into disobedience. Here is an example: suppose some people know evil; we turn them away from it and cure them of it, because it is a sickness, and it is mercy in the sense that they do not fall into sickness at the outset. So there are two observations pointing to the two parts: the first observation: the Qur'anic method was sent down as prevention for one who has not fallen into disobedience. The second observation: the method contains the treatment for one who has fallen into disobedience. The Truth, the Exalted, specifies who benefits from the Qur'anic method as prevention and treatment, saying: ﴿... and guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [Yusuf: 111]; that is, those who believe in one God who created them and the universe, and set for mankind laws to safeguard their lives. It is logical that the believer hears His words and implements them, because He set the method to which you can return in everything that protects your life. So if you are a believer in God, take the guidance, and take the mercy. We ask God that we be granted all of this.
